Their combined presence poured through every star, strengthening... the very fabric of existence.
"This enemy is not one of us.
He is a foreign will—a parasite feeding on the life of the Universe.
He seeks to devour the Worlds, to turn the living into shadows of himself."
Seraphielle’s wings opened wide again, scattering divine light across creation.
"But we will not allow it."
Ul’Thakar raised his hand, his shadow stretching across the Veil like a colossal storm.
"He will learn what it means to trespass upon another god’s domain."
Equarios lowered his gaze, hands clasped.
"From this moment forth, the Four Infinities act as one."
Orravyn’s book glowed.
"And the Universe itself shall be our witness."
The Veil pulsed, splitting into four shimmering colors—gold, black, blue, and silver-white—each carrying the words of one Infinity.
Seraphielle stepped forward,
"To every being who carries even a spark of light within—
Rise.
Do not let your heart falter, for this battle is not between gods alone.
It is the battle of creation against the void."
Her voice warmed the air of a million worlds.
"The Light will protect as it used to.
It will guide, it will heal, it will stand as the first wall between you and the threat that seeks to consume you.
And when the threat approaches, remember—
Light does not retreat."
Ul’Thakar’s crimson gaze gleamed from behind the veil of smoke.
"To those who live in shadow, who bear and reflect pain, who walk unseen—
You are not forgotten.
You are my children too."
The skies of countless worlds dimmed—not from fear, but from reverence.
"Let the Universe know not to mistake stillness for weakness.
Let the Universe know that the Darkness shields just as the Light burns.
And when the invader comes, we shall show him what true fear feels like."
His smirk flashed across a thousand horizons.
"Let the foreign god taste the despair of the night that even stars bow before."
Equarios extended his hands.
Rings of blue and silver light expanded outward like ripples in water.
"And to those who seek peace, to those who uphold reason, to those who heal instead of harm—
Stand firm.
Do not give in to panic, nor to the whispers that promise power for chaos."
He turned his gaze upon the countless worlds watching him.
"The Anomaly feeds on imbalance.
It thrives on destruction, confusion, and despair.
Deny it that nourishment.
Stay united.
Live.
And in living, you wound him more than any blade could."
Finally, Orravyn spoke again, his tone serene but infinite, carrying the weight of a certain... inevitability.
"And to those who remember, who record, who wonder—
Your duty is knowledge.
Watch.
Learn.
Endure."
His book turned again, pages glowing as if every moment in history was being rewritten before their eyes.
"Because in the end, even time bows to those who understand it."
He smiled faintly.
"The Anomaly believes himself to be Infinite.
But Infinity is not longevity—it is meaning.
And meaning... belongs to us."
FWHOOOSH
As the Four finished their... vows, a new light filled the skies—not from them, but from... the Universe itself.
Every world pulsed with color.
Every river glittered.
Every sun burned... warmer.
Galaxies tilted slightly in their courses, aligning like petals turning toward sunlight.
The hearts of the living—mortals, beasts, cultivators alike—trembled as they heard something beneath the Infinities’ voices—
A deeper, far more... older sound.
The heartbeat of creation.
Pulsing with... life again.
The Universe.
It was relishing in joy, a strong, impossibly recognizable joy.
Across all the worlds, people fell to their knees—staring upward in awe.
Even the World Leaders, arrogant beings who ruled their people like gods, bowed their heads, for they understood:
This was not mere words or speech.
It was...
A historical moment—
A moment that would change the history of their Universe—for the worse or for the better.
A moment they were all part of.
And as the very Universe celebrated their words with them—the Infinities’ voices rose again.
"To the one who devours our worlds—
To the thief who calls himself Anomaly—
Hear this."
The Veil trembled, every color blending into a single blazing brilliance that stretched from end to end of the cosmos.
"You have taken what is not yours.
You have crossed the boundary of creation.
You have sown despair in a home that is not your own."
Ul’Thakar’s shadow spread wider, like a storm embracing the stars.
"You wished for gods to notice you.
Now you have our attention."
Seraphielle’s wings flared, her light bursting into the hearts of suns.
"You wished for power beyond your Universe.
Now you shall learn what power truly is."
Equarios’s halo turned like a vast celestial wheel.
"You wished for chaos.
You will find balance instead."
And Eternity’s book closed with a soft snap that echoed across worlds.
"You wished to write your story into ours.
But this Chapter... belongs to us."
Their combined voices thundered across the fabric of space.
"Let all beings bear witness—
The Four Infinities stand united.
And this...
is our declaration of War."
As those words echoed throughout the Universe, the bright light began to fade.
The Veil started dissolving.
But before it vanished completely, Eternity’s gaze turned—looking through the stars, beyond what was... comprehensible.
And this time—his tone changed to something... softer, more... uncertain.
After all, this time, he wasn’t talking to mortals, but to someone... far... different.
Someone far more... complex.
"To the Seer who watches all paths—
We call to you.
The threads of fate are knotting again.
If you can still hear us, lend us your sight."
Then, Light stepped forward, adding her own words as her voice was tinged with both reverence and challenge.
"To the Fifth Infinity—the one who turned from us.
Your silence has lasted long enough.
If your will still lies with this Universe,
Prove it now."
And finally, the last voice came, the voice that belonged to Darkness—but this time, it wasn’t a call.
It was a warning.
"And to the one who hides beneath the ashes of Chaos...
If you still exist, Zylarith Chaosveil...
Then rise."
The word ’rise’ rippled through creation like a curse and a prayer combined.
Every world shuddered, every star flickered, every being lowered their head as Balance’s calm and steady words closed the moment—
"The stage is set.
The pieces will move again.
May the Universe guide the worthy."
And then... silence.
Absolute silence fell all over the Universe.
The Veil vanished, leaving only the memory of light and shadow in the sky.
But the worlds did not return to their old rhythm.
They pulsed, alive.
Every corner of existence glowed faintly, as though blessed by something divine.
In that quiet village under the blue-lit sky, the same boy who had looked up before was still standing there, his knees trembling.
The fire before him burned bright again, almost playful.
The air shimmered with warmth that shouldn’t exist at night.
He pressed a hand to his chest, feeling his heart beat faster—and for the first time in his life, he smiled.
Somewhere deep in his soul, he knew.
The gods had not abandoned them.
They had simply been waiting for the right moment to return.
And that moment...
had finally come.

chapters.title: Chapter 2223: More Information.
paragraphs: [The stage is set.
The pieces will move again.
May the Universe guide the worthy.]
As those words echoed throughout the space, a long, deafening silence followed.
For a good while, no one spoke until finally—
"Now this looks interesting."
Astaria commented with an amused grin, her eyes reflecting a strong fighting spirit. She too wanted to participate in thisgame.
And it wasn’t just her—
"Indeed."
Her master and sister, Vyriana, had the same look on her face.
"They called everyone to the party. I am offended that I wasn’t called."
The Dragon pouted and then—
"You talk as if you were out there hunting the Supreme Borns. They probably don’t even know someone like you exists."
Edda snickered, making the Dragon’s mouth twitch, but at the end of the day, there was nothing she could say against those words.
She had started to feel it as well.
As time had passed, she... she had become... irrelevant.

She was once a Sovereign, a being who Nux relied upon, a being who was a major part of Nux’s life, and while she knew Nux would one day surpass her, she always believed that even then—she would remain relevant.
She would remain someone Nux knew he could rely on, and for a good while, she did maintain that position.
She was one of the first Transcendents amongst her sisters, and just a few centuries ago, she could still keep up with Nux and spar with him to a somewhat equal level.
But now...?
Now it had all changed.
Nux had gone... beyond what she could handle. Let alone spar with him at a decent level—even if she used all her might—she... she wasn’t even strong enough to make him lift his finger in response.
The difference between them was now... too vast for her to even think about someday reducing it.
But...
That wasn’t even the worst part.
Even before, Vyriana knew that if Nux faced her seriously using all the strength he had, she was nowhere close to defeating him, but that still didn’t stop her because he still relied upon her.
There were still things he needed her to do, worlds he wanted her to destroy, beings he wanted her to defeat.
But now...
Now things were different.
Now, Nux had his own immortal army, and that army had... Eternals.
Yes, Eternal-level beings now served Nux, and while this had helped him quite a bit... for Vyriana...
It felt... overwhelming.
She felt... useless.
Whatever she could do, those Eternals could do better—far more efficiently.

These Eternals had nothing to fear. Nux had altered their minds in a way that pointless emotions like fear, anger, pride—all emotions that could slow a being down and stop him from moving efficiently—no longer existed.
It wouldn’t be wrong to call these beings puppets, puppets who existed solely to fulfil Nux’s orders.
And all this...
This made her helpless.
The worst part?
Nux had no fear when it came to losing these puppets.
He had been experimenting with this for centuries now and finally, after his Universe was complete, it was done.
Vyriana—or any of Nux’s wives—shared a connection with him, a connection that was supported by Lane’s Law. This connection allowed Nux or his wives to be reborn in case of some mishap.
Basically, Nux, through his connection to his wives, could be reborn near any of them, and his wives, through their connection, could be reborn near Nux.
And while this connection was quite beneficial, it came with its own... disadvantages.

This connected all their lives, meaning that a being strong enough to sense and interact with this connection had a slight chance of being able to kill Nux and all his wives just by getting their hands on even one of them.
Of course, Nux himself was a Universe—which is considered quite a ’heavy’ entity—so being able to influence his or even his wife’s life just by interacting with this connection was... difficult.
It required... power.
An almost... unlimited amount of power.
Something only... an Infinity might have access to.
Before, Nux didn’t quite care, after all, he knew an Infinity wasn’t going to make a move anytime soon.
But later, as he began to challenge Infinities himself, directly calling them out in the open, provoking them in front of the entire Universe—
That began to change.
Now that the chances of an Infinity attacking them were considerably higher...
This connection, which he had also shared with his subordinates, turning them into immortals, had become... less of a benefit and more of a sword hanging near their throats.
This was also the reason that back then, Nux removed all his subordinates from this connection network.
But even then, he hadn’t given up.
Even before removing his subordinates from the connection, he was already thinking of a way around it.
A way through which he could keep the benefits and... lose the downsides.
And once his Universe was complete, he finally found a way.
Souls.
After completing his Universe and gaining an even better control over it, Nux... learned something new.
He learned about Souls. He learned how to... interact with them in a much better way than what he knew before.
Before, he only used souls for torture, since a being’s soul feels multiple times more pain than his body, but... that was the crudest use one could possibly think of for something so... precious.
The soul was... immortal.
It didn’t matter if it was the soul of a mortal, a cultivator, or even a mindless beast—all these souls—unless something unexpected happened—were... immortal.
The souls did not die; they simply returned to the Universe to be reborn again.
And Nux...
After becoming a Complete Universe, he too could access a soul that was a part of his Universe, like other normal Universes could.
Yes, Nux too now held the power to reincarnate a being from his Universe. As for how he used this power—
Whether he reincarnated the said soul in another world, giving it a new, different life as a mindless beast, or an intelligent being, or even an inanimate living entity—
Or... he reincarnated—or in this case—revived the said soul into the same being it once was, without erasing its ’memories’...
It was all in Nux’s hands.
So yes, now, after completing his Universe, Nux no longer needed Lane’s Law for his subordinates.

Of course, this did not mean Lane’s Law was useless; he still needed it to revive their ’bodies’, but since the ’soul’ was no longer part of the deal, the connection was no longer between Nux’s soul and his subordinate’s soul.
It was between...
Nux’s body and his subordinate’s body.
And... no matter how strong the enemy who captured his subordinate was... killing Nux’s body, which had been reinforced with tens of High-Level Worlds, was... difficult even for an Infinity.
And even then—
If they somehow managed to hurt or even destroy Nux’s body through their connection, he would simply...
Revive again.

Yes, Nux could now use his subordinates without a tinge of fear or worry in his head. Even if all the Infinities captured his subordinates, it wouldn’t make a difference to him, since they wouldn’t find anything.
Heck, they couldn’t even trace that connection back and forcefully enter his Universe, because that too wasn’t possible unless he created an opening himself.
This was also the reason that even after challenging the Infinities, he was letting his subordinates roam throughout the Main Universe without any worries about the Infinities acting.
No, hewantedthe Infinities to act.
He wanted to see the extent of their powers so he could come up with plans of his own.
"We need to get stronger."
As Vyriana was thinking all this, suddenly, Amaya commented.

The devourer, just like the Dragon, was facing the same helplessness. She knew Nux. She knew that now that he had that immortal army, he wouldn’t let any of them leave the Universe, and while she loved his protective nature, being unable to offer him any help at all was... eating her from the inside.
"As if that would change anything."
But Felberta shook her head, and once the women turned towards her, the first wife chuckled softly,
"The Infinities have challenged us openly. We are facing the strongest enemies in the Universe, enemies we and Nux know nothing about.
No matter how strong we become, he will never let us leave.
Forget about it."
Amaya wanted to counter her words but... there was nothing she could say.
"She is right."
Riona nodded as well.
She then glanced at her daughter and—
"Instead of thinking about leaving, it would be better to think of a way to help Nux deal with the Infinities,
To gather... more information."
"How do we do that?"
Rune asked. Even Nux, with all his means, couldn’t gather any information regarding the Infinities till now; how weretheysupposed to do it?
But then suddenly—
"What if..."
Another voice was heard.
"I call Father?"
The Vampire spoke.

chapters.title: Chapter 2224: We can use Zylarith Chaosveil to grow stronger.
paragraphs: "Instead of thinking about leaving, it would be better to think of a way to help Nux deal with the Infinities,
To gather... more information."
"How do we do that?"
Rune asked. Even Nux, with all his means, couldn’t gather any information regarding the Infinities till now—how were they supposed to do it?
But then suddenly—
"What if... I call Father?"
Suddenly, another voice was heard.
A voice that had a way out.
All the women present turned towards the Vampire, and Aeliana pointed at the frozen screen that was hovering in front of them, the screen that still showed the four Infinities.
"They said it themselves, didn’t they?
The stage is set, it is time for the pieces to move again.
My Father is... one of those pieces."
Aeliana spoke, her eyes shining with a new intensity.
"What are you trying to say?"
Melia narrowed her eyes at those words, and Aeliana—
"They called him, did they not?
Why not let Father have... a talk with them?
Who knows?
This might help us find something we otherwise wouldn’t have known."
"Don’t be foolish."
Amaya raised her voice, instantly snapping at the Vampire.
"Lord Azriel is no longer an Infinity. He is not as strong as he used to be. Getting in contact with the Infinities..."
Amaya didn’t need to finish those words.
"And don’t forget, Lord Azriel was the one who defended Nux from the Infinities for the first time.
The Infinities saw him, but they still called for him.
That call wasn’t simple; they must have thought a lot about it.
It is... not safe."
Vyriana shook her head as well.
She too was against this idea.
"I am not saying Father has to go there."
Aeliana, however, didn’t give in.
"I do not want to put my father’s life at stake for information that could or could not be useful.
I am not that selfish."
The Vampire shook her head, looking at the women.
"What I am saying is Father can leave a message—find a way to communicate with the Infinities without actually meeting them."
"They won’t trust him."
Thyra shook her head.
After all, she too would never trust a being who once helped an enemy and wasn’t willing to meet her.
But Aeliana was already prepared with an answer.
"They never will."
She smiled lightly.
"The situation in front of us is... ambiguous.
And it is the same for everyone—
In fact, it must be even worse for our enemies.
After all, while we still have significant information about them, they... they know absolutely nothing.
Yes, they were correct about us being from another Universe, but... what do they even know about our Universe?
They have absolutely nothing.

It wouldn’t be that odd to think that they truly believe we come from a completely different, independent, functioning Universe that was once like theirs before Nux became its ruler—or maybe even now, they believe Nux is just one of the enemies they are facing while others are still in hiding.
That is how big the information gap is.
At the very least, we know who our enemies are and what their numbers are.
But they?
They are clueless.
To make things even worse, unlike us—who move with absolute trust in each other, knowing the other would throw even their life for our sake if the situation arose—
They are four separate entities, four beings each with their own goals, their own schemes and... the chance of readily backstabbing others if it benefits them.
They are not even proper allies.
If anything, they are all using each other, and they all fear being used by each other.
To them, this is the worst possible scenario, a scenario where their minds are overwhelmed by the sheer number of variables they need to deal with.
So much so that in this uncertain, ambiguous situation filled with variables, they decided to...
Add even more variables."
"Making it more complex so others do not understand it either, huh..."
Amaya muttered, slowly understanding the thought process.
"Exactly."
Aeliana nodded.
"They fear not comprehending the situation and being used by others, so instead, they decided to make everything even more complicated so others too do not understand anything and feel the same fear.
That is all there is to it.
None of the Infinities has any ’plans’, and even if they do, we do not have to do anything—other Infinities will do everything in their power to make sure they fail."
The Vampire laughed.
"But I do not understand."
Ember, however, frowned. While she understood the gist of what Aeliana was trying to say, what she did not understand was—
"What does all of this have to do with requesting Lord Azriel to get in contact with the Infinities?"
The Dragon asked, and Aeliana—
"Nothing."
She just smiled.
"They are moving ambiguously, so I thoughtwhy don’t we participate as well?
Father now has a way to hide his presence from even the Universe itself despite being the Universe’s Child. There is no way the Infinities would be able to find him unless he wants them to."
The Vampire was confident.
"Of course, that is all to say this is merely a suggestion. I would still need to talk to Father to know what he thinks of it all.
I wouldn’t be surprised if he waves his hand, calls it all a bother, and cuts the call."
She muttered, and the women who were hearing her and knew her father all rolled their eyes.
Yeah right, like that man would ever cut his daughter’s call on his own.
Every single one of them had the same thought in their head, after all, they had seen that look in that man’s eyes whenever he talked to Aeliana.
There was no way that fool for his daughter would ever treat his daughter that way.
"We can ask Lord Azriel for help. I do not deny it."
Finally, Amaya gave in as well.

Everything Aeliana said made certain sense. The Vampire wasn’t expecting anything from this move; one could even say she was just playing along with the game the Infinities were playing, making it... more fun.
But if they were fortunate enough, this harmless little game might... give them something important.
Of course, what this something was, she did not know, but Amaya didn’t completely reject the idea of getting something useful out of it.
Yes, it was a blind shot.
A shot that they knew would not hurt them in return, so there was no loss in making this move.
"Should I call him now?"
Aeliana asked, her eyes brightening instantly. It had been a long time since she had talked to him anyway—she was missing him.

But right now—
"Zylarith Chaosveil— that name troubles me. We still haven’t found the answer to the previous issue either."

The Succubus asked.
"I understand they wish to make things more complicated but... the more the complications, the more Chaos grows and...

"We can use Zylarith Chaosveil to grow stronger.
Strong enough to help Nux."

To gather... more information."
"How do we do that?"

But then suddenly—
"What if...
I call Father?"
Suddenly, another voice was heard.
A voice that had a way out.
All the women present turned towards the Vampire, and Aeliana pointed at the frozen screen that was hovering in front of them, the screen that still showed the four Infinities.
"They said it themselves, didn’t they?
The stage is set, it is time for the pieces to move again.
My Father is... one of those pieces."
Aeliana spoke, her eyes shining with a new intensity.
"What are you trying to say?"
Melia narrowed her eyes at those words, and Aeliana—
"They called him, did they not?
Why not let Father have... a talk with them?
Who knows?

Amaya raised her voice, instantly snapping at the Vampire.

Amaya didn’t need to finish those words.

"I am not saying Father has to go there."
Aeliana, however, didn’t give in.
"I do not want to put my father’s life at stake for information that could or could not be useful.
I am not that selfish."
The Vampire shook her head, looking at the women.
"What I am saying is Father can leave a message—find a way to communicate with the Infinities without actually meeting them."
"They won’t trust him."
Thyra shook her head.
After all, she too would never trust a being who once helped an enemy and wasn’t willing to meet her.
But Aeliana was already prepared with an answer.
"They never will."
She smiled lightly.

In fact, it must be even worse for our enemies.

They have absolutely nothing.

That is how big the information gap is.
At the very least, we know who our enemies are and what their numbers are.
But they?
They are clueless.
To make things even worse, unlike us—who move with absolute trust in each other, knowing the other would throw even their life for our sake if the situation arose—
They are four separate entities, four beings each with their own goals, their own schemes and... the chance of readily backstabbing others if it benefits them.
They are not even proper allies.
If anything, they are all using each other, and they all fear being used by each other.
To them, this is the worst possible scenario, a scenario where their minds are overwhelmed by the sheer number of variables they need to deal with.
So much so that in this uncertain, ambiguous situation filled with variables, they decided to...
Add even more variables."
"Making it more complex so others do not understand it either, huh..."
Amaya muttered, slowly understanding the thought process.
"Exactly."
Aeliana nodded.
"They fear not comprehending the situation and being used by others, so instead, they decided to make everything even more complicated so others too do not understand anything and feel the same fear.
That is all there is to it.
None of the Infinities has any ’plans’, and even if they do, we do not have to do anything—other Infinities will do everything in their power to make sure they fail."
The Vampire laughed.
"But I do not understand."
Ember, however, frowned.

"What does all of this have to do with requesting Lord Azriel to get in contact with the Infinities?"
The Dragon asked, and Aeliana—
"Nothing."
She just smiled.

Father now has a way to hide his presence from even the Universe itself despite being the Universe’s Child.
There is no way the Infinities would be able to find him unless he wants them to."

I wouldn’t be surprised if he waves his hand, calls it all a bother, and cuts the call."

chapters.title: Chapter 2225: Why don’t we... ask my Father instead?
paragraphs: "He might also be the solution to the problem we are currently facing."
"What do you mean...?"
The Dragon narrowed her eyes at those words, andLyriana—
"We can use Zylarith Chaosveil to grow stronger.
Strong enough to help Nux."
She spoke with a solemn look on her face and her words echoed inside every woman’s mind.
Amaya asked, all her attention now on Lyriana, if it was something that could make them strong enough to help Nux then...
"We need to devour him."
Lyriana spoke, and in an instant, every woman present there froze.
"Devour... Zylarith...?"
Amaya blinked at the absurdity of the statement, but the more she thought about it, the more... benefits she was able to see.
And seeing the light in the devourer’s eyes changing, Lyriana continued—
"It would take only a few centuries for you, Vyriana, Aeliana, Astaria and I to break through and become Eternals.
And although as Eternals, we will be able to help Nux to some extent, we all know that alone won’t be enough.

Even now, Nux can defeat Eternals as if they are mere bugs. Even that Auren, the Strongest Child of Light, who is known as one of the strongest Eternals in the Universe, wasn’t a match for him and was knocked out in less than a second.
Even if it is us in his stead, with the level Nux has reached right now, it wouldn’t be any different.
We...
We need to become even stronger."
The Elf’s eyes shined intensely as she said the next words.
"Stronger than an Eternal."
The women present narrowed their eyes, listening properly. The Elf paused briefly, gathering her thoughts, and then—
"But our Universe’s Cultivation Bridge has a restriction."
"We do not have a way to go beyond the Eternal Stage."
Astaria muttered. She, like others, also knew about this problem, but since she was only a Transcendent right now, she had decided not to think about it till she became an Eternal.
But now...
Her thoughts were changing.
If she was right, then what Lyriana was trying to say was—

"If we devour Zylarith, we will have all the knowledge we require regarding the Infinity Stage, just like how our Cultivation Bridge grew once Nux learned about the Eternal Stage. Once he devours Zylarith,
He can grow the Cultivation Bridge, opening up the path to... the Infinity Stage.
Allowing us...
To become Infinities as well."
The Elf completed her words, and even though almost all the women had already predicted what she was going to say, those words still sent shivers down their spines.
"By then, the enemies wouldn’t even matter.
Even without Nux, the Four Infinities would be... helpless against us. And while I do agree this would take time—
But if we become Infinity...
Then instead of Nux, who has been protecting and helping us grow all this time—we would be doing all this for him instead.

One by one, we will kill the enemy Infinities and let Nux devour them, and then their Worlds, and finally—after us—Nux too will break through, reaching a stage no being in the entire Multiverse has ever reached."
The more Lyriana spoke, the grander her words felt. The women, who had stayed in the background for far too long, finally saw... a ray of hope.
Hope that they too... could be useful to Nux, like they all once desired to be.
They too would be able to give back everything he had done for them and show him just how much they cherished him.
Vyriana, who was already imagining holding that Light Infinity by her throat, grinned. Her golden eyes shining intensely as she imagined an all-out battle of Infinities.
The Final Battle that would decide it all.
The Final Battle where—not Nux—but she would lead the charge.
And the more tempting part?
Lyriana wasn’t even finished yet.
"Nux’s Cultivation Bridge is uncertain."
She began. Now the women were far more attentive to her words because they too had begun to dream.
"Even now, he does not know what makes him strong. ’Acting how a Universe would’ isn’t a concrete answer either.
And as he is growing stronger and stronger, the number of ’Universe-like things’ he can do is... decreasing.
Finding a way to get stronger from this stage onward is... uncertain. He can only rely on his Universe to grow naturally. Not many things from the Main Universe can actually help him now.
And while devouring the Main Universe’s High Level Worlds helps to some extent, that too comes with a strong risk of the Infinities surrounding and ambushing him.
But...
Now that we already have Vexarion, Nux would have no need to leave his Universe once we have Zylarith too.
That way, Nux would no longer need to put himself at risk against the Infinities, and we... we will have all the time in the Universe to catch up to him and... eventually surpass him.
Of course, all of it is possible only after we catch Zylarith. As to how we do it...
Although I do have some ideas, none of them guarantees anything."
Lyriana spoke, and once again, complete silence fell over the place as the women’s thoughts ran wild.
And no, these thoughts weren’t just about capturing Zylarith, defeating Infinities, and helping Nux...
While some of them indeed had such... innocent thoughts... others were... a little different.
The words ’surpassing Nux’ were echoing in some of the women’s heads and... the possibility of becoming stronger than Nux after such a long time placed an... evil grin on their faces.
The pictures in their minds were not pretty at all.
Pictures that would make even Nux gulp if he saw them—of course, that isn’t to say he wouldn’t be looking forward to it.
But right now—
The most important thing—even more important than discussing the other Infinities—was to find Zylarith.
"How about we use her?"
Thyra suggested.
The problem was that Zylarith was in his Soul Form. Even the Universe itself is unable to detect him, let alone them, who had no way to track him down.
They did, however, have one link with Zylarith in their hands.
Sharnoth Nocthys.
Zylarith had the power to have complete control over her body once she activates her Body of Chaos, so if she makes an appearance, the chances of him appearing were... quite high.
Of course, as for him controlling her body, Sharnoth was now connected to their Universe. Even if he takes control over her body—
They could simply call her back and he would be helpless, so they weren’t putting Sharnoth in danger either.
Thyra didn’t see anything wrong with this,
"We cannot do that."
Felberta, however, shook her head.
"We do not know to what extent he can control her body and whether Zylarith needs to be close by to control her.
For all we know, he could control her from wherever he is, and we would still fail to track him down.
Not to mention there are also the Infinities.
They know Sharnoth is now with us. The moment Sharnoth appears, the Infinities might make a move too, and then the situation would become far more complicated than we can handle.
And Nux..."
Felberta paused for a moment and then—
"He won’t agree to it."
At those words, Skyla laughed.
"Mhm, Sharnoth isn’t just Sharnoth,
She’s Sister Sharnoth now!"
"How long are they going to spend in there anyway?"
Aisha jumped into the conversation too, pouting at the fact that she wasn’t there with them.
"She is an Eternal, so I believe she would last longer than most."
Eisheth commented. The women couldn’t peek in there since Nux put the restrictions, so all they could do was guess.
"Should we go visit?"
Allura asked, her eyes lightening as she imagined the amusing sight and the flustered Sharnoth.
"Shouldn’t we... worry more about Zylarith right now..."
Lyriana muttered with a deadpan look on her face.
The Elf had already gotten used to the conversation drifting away from the topic at any moment now; she wasn’t even surprised at this point.
But then suddenly,
"Why don’t we... ask my Father instead?"
Aeliana spoke up.
The women turned towards her and the Vampire frowned—
"Why put so much effort into catching Zylarith? Sure, devouring him might give us some information about the four Infinities, but that information would be trillions of years old.
It is not worth it to go through so much effort for such outdated information when the main information that we need can be gathered from other sources, without having to go through so much trouble."
"Are you suggesting we ask your Father to let Nux read his memories?"
Lyriana asked, and Aeliana nodded.
"We need information to grow our Cultivation Bridge, do we not?
My Father was once an Infinity too. Why not use his help?"
"It won’t work."
Lyriana shook her head.

"It might have if Nux read his memories before, but now he cannot, since Lord Azriel is now connected to the Universe. Peering into his mind would alert the Universe, which would... result in the Universe reacting strongly and...
Killing Lord Azriel for betraying it."

chapters.title: Chapter 2226: He’s finally awake.
paragraphs: "My Father was once an Infinity too, why not use his help?"
Aeliana asked and Lyriana—
"It won’t work."
She shook her head.

"It might have if Nux read his memories before, but now he cannot since Lord Azriel is now connected to the Universe. Peering into his mind would alert the Universe, which would... result in the Universe reacting strongly and...
Killing Lord Azriel for betraying it."
"What...?"
The Vampire blinked.

"When I was discussing all this with Nux, he too had the same idea. He contacted Lord Azriel and he told him that now that he was the Universe’s Child, the connection between him and the Universe is far stronger than the connection the Universe shares with its other connections.
So the moment Nux, who has no connection with the Universe, tries to read his memories, the Universe will sense his presence and understand that its own Child is working with the foreign enemy.
And of course...
What happens next is..."
Lavinia didn’t think it was right to repeat the same thing. Aeliana, however, frowned.
"Didn’t Father’s new Law make him independent of the Universe?"

From what Azriel told her, there weren’t many things the Universe could do against him even though he was now its child. This was the reason she was so comfortable constantly being in contact with her father despite no longer being part of the Main Universe.
"Lord Azriel said he isn’t sure whether the Universe holds the power to actually kill him, but enraging it was not a wise option.
Also..."
The Elf hesitated for a moment, but seeing the look in the Vampire’s eyes, she just sighed and continued—
"He said he is disgusted by the idea of having Nux read his memories and told Nux to deal with his problems on his own.
And he warned not to bother him again, else he is going to take his daughter away."
The Elf added at the end, and the rest of the women who heard those words just rolled their eyes again.
Still trying to find excuses to take her away, as if he is going to let it happen.
But this time, not every woman had the same thought. One had a different one.
What’s with the empty warnings, just take her away.
Amaya thought inwardly, her dark eyes getting even darker as she stared at Aeliana.
"Wait..."
Then suddenly, Rune frowned, staring at Lyriana.
"When you were talking to Nux about this...
Does this mean you have already discussed all this with Nux?"
The Cat woman asked, her frown deepening with every passing moment.

"What gave you the idea that I would discuss something with you first before going to Nux?"
And the moment she said those words, Rune...
"Right. I didn’t think that through."
The Cat woman nodded too, shaking her head at her foolish question.
The Elf nodded back and then—
"What did Nux say when you were discussing this matter?"
Amaya asked.
She wanted to know what Nux was thinking. Of course, she was now going to have another private discussion regarding this with Nux, but it would still be better to gain some insights and prepare well.
Lavinia, however, answered with a frown,
"He... he frowned when I mentioned Zylarith’s name, saying how he couldn’t be trusted."
"He is an enemy. Of course he cannot be trusted."
Ember commented with a frown too. What was the Elf talking about?
"No, not like that..."
Lyriana tried to explain, but for a moment, she felt... stumped, and that was when Eisheth spoke up.
"There are too many lies in Zylarith’s story."
The women tilted their heads, once again turning their attention to the Succubus, and the Succubus continued—
"When he first appeared, he introduced himself as Nux’s Soul Father, a being who created the Universe, and while what he said was true...
That time, he tried to make you all believe that there were more than Four Infinities in the Four Supreme Worlds.
He mentioned how the Supreme Worlds had multiple races, each race had a Progenitor, and every Progenitor was an Infinity.

He framed the story in a way where he stated that he too shared his World’s Energy with a few other Progenitors, and he also stated this was what made Lord Azriel so special, that he had most of Yrniel’s Energy, making him... the strongest Infinity in the Universe.
But now that things have been clarified...
We all know that those words are... meaningless."
"Are you saying... that Lord Azriel was not the strongest Infinity in the Universe?"
Vyriana asked with a frown. Aeliana too listened carefully, but Eisheth just shook her head.
"First, these are not my words. These were Nux’s. I too had a talk with him regarding Zylarith since my instincts warned me about him.
And Nux nodded at my words, saying that he felt the same.
Also, this isn’t about Lord Azriel."
Eisheth spoke, looking at Aeliana.
"It doesn’t matter if he was the strongest or not. What Nux was trying to say is, none of what Zylarith said can be trusted.

Lord Azriel may be strong, or even the strongest, but to say that the reason he was at the level he was, was because he had complete support of Yrniel while he and other Infinities had to share their Worlds’ Energies with other Progenitors was a complete lie.
Nux also said that when they first met him, Zylarith purposefully downplayed him in front of Lord Azriel despite himself being known as the Strongest Infinity in the history of the Universe."
"I don’t understand."
Suddenly, Evane, who mostly stayed silent during these conversations, spoke up as well.
"The enemy lied, why make such a big deal about it?
Why would one be... honest with his enemies?"
"Because back then Zylarith had no strong reason to lie."
This time, the one who answered this question was Amaya, recalling that time she ’interrogated’ that man.
"That time, he wanted Nux to follow him, so revealing that he was once the strongest existence in the entire Universe would have been more beneficial instead.
Or maybe...
He never wanted Nux to follow him."
"What...?"
Evane narrowed her eyes at those words and Amaya—
"I always found it strange. Zylarith, according to his words, was waiting for Nux for trillions of years, yet...
When Nux first appeared, instead of investigating him to make sure everything went exactly as he planned, he... said the thing that would offend Nux—the key part of his grand plan, the most?"
"Are you saying... he did that on purpose...?"
Aeliana spoke, her tone now much grimmer than before.
But Amaya just shook her head,
"I do not know.
It could be a careless mistake he made in his arrogance. Trillions of years doesn’t excuse his arrogance, it only amplifies it.
But at the same time...
He is not a being one could underestimate either—especially since even the Four Infinities seem quite wary of him.
We still cannot consider the possibility that he did it on purpose, and if that is indeed the case...
Then none of us know how much of what is currently happening has he predicted beforehand."
Amaya muttered in a solemn tone, and Eisheth nodded at her words.
"Nux said something similar as well.
He said nothing related to Zylarith can be trusted. Every time he is involved, we need to think multiple times from different perspectives, not just from the perspective he showed us.
Sometimes...
I feel... Nux is more wary of Zylarith than he is of the Four Infinities."
"He is right to be."
Ember nodded at those words.
"A hidden enemy will always be more threatening than the one who is out in the open. And then...
Then there is the Seer too."
The Dragon mentioned another name—name that... confused them all. After all, just like Zylarith’s, her actions, her goals aren’t clear either.
Not to mention—
There was still that ’third gift’ left out of three gifts she had prepared for Nux and... not even Nux knew what it was going to be.
Suddenly, while they were discussing everything, Felberta suddenly laughed out loud, attracting the attention of the group.
Then, a nostalgic look appeared on the Eldraeth Progenitor’s face and—
"We really did come this far, huh..."
She muttered in a low voice.

"To think the countryside nobles, who didn’t even know cultivation above the King Stages existed, are now... talking about beings far beyond anyone’s comprehension and will soon be actively facing them...
We...
We have indeed come a long way."
A strange smile then appeared on her face and—
"I did not think my... the decision of taking in a weak-looking handsome boy—a decision I made after being influenced by my friends’ words—would bring me... here."
She spoke, looking around the entire Universe that she could confidently call hers.
Just like her, the rest of the women began to remember the past as well, romanticizing it for a moment, well, everyone but... Shadow.
Her focus was on something else.
"He’s finally awake."
The woman grinned.

chapters.title: Chapter 2227: You brought this upon yourself.
paragraphs: "He’s finally awake."

While the rest of the women were recalling their past, the time when they first met Nux, remembering their first interaction with him—interactions where some fell in love at first sight, some were suspicious, some were curious, and some just found the ’boy’ interesting—Shadow had something entirely different in her mind.
After all, Nux had promised it would be her turn next.
She had been waiting, waiting ever since Nux had completed his Universe and she had gained a new body.
And now...
It was finally time, time when she could give even her new body to the man she loved.
As that thought appeared in her mind, Shadow grinned, then, without waiting for even the slightest second, shadows surrounded her body and she disappeared.
"Where did she go?"
"Wait..."
Her disappearance quickly attracted others’ attention, pulling them out of their reveries.
"She... did she go to him?"
Aisha asked, confused.
"But I still can’t sense him."
Riona frowned.
They all had a connection to Nux, but he had temporarily sealed that connection to spend some time alone with Sharnoth.
Shadow shouldn’t be any different...
Or at least, that’s what they thought but...
"Her connection to him got stronger again."
Amaya spoke with an ugly expression on her face. Other women were jealous too but then—
"Should we go as well?"
Allura suggested with a playful smile on her face.
"Go where? Nux promised her. There’s no point and she definitely won’t share."
Aisha snorted.
Yes, she obviously tried to share; she tried it the instant Nux promised Shadow, but the woman did not listen.
She was quite selfish.
"Who said I am talking about Shadow."
Allura’s smile widened.
"She isn’t fun but...
Someone else must be, especially right now."
She spoke and suddenly, the rest of the women—especially Edda, Aisha and Eisheth—grinned as well.
"Shall we?"
Allura repeated her question and this time, the three women nodded and all four of them disappeared at the same time.
The remaining women shook their heads at the immature behaviour.
Obviously, unlike the four, they weren’t too interested in such matters, so in the next moment—
They too disappeared, following Allura and the others because, well, they had nothing better to do either.
Teasing and intimidating the new joinee sounded quite fun.
On the other side of Nux’s Universe, inside the room of the mansion he had created just for Sharnoth alone, Nux lay on the bed with his head supported by his hand.
In front of him was Sharnoth, who was now resting.
The Chaos Heir’s eyes were closed, her breathing uneven, and her body...
Nux had covered it with blankets.
After all, he had no intention of going further, not when he knew the state Sharnoth’s body and her mind were in, and covering the temptation was the only way for him to stop.
But even then, even after he had covered her body, he... still couldn’t turn away because Sharnoth...
Her face covered with that light sweat, and some of her damp, messy hair, looked... absolutely mesmerizing.
It was a sight he could stare at for hours without feeling tired at all.
But...
This wasn’t the luxury he could have because—
Boom
"Nux! It’s my turn now!"
The doors of the room were shot open and a woman barged in with a smile that did not suit her dignified appearance one bit.
"Shadow...?"
The moment the woman appeared, Nux blinked.
His focus was all on Sharnoth, so he truly did not know Shadow was coming and Shadow—
"You are finally done, it’s my turn now, let’s go."
She spoke without a shred of shame as she walked towards him, her beautiful eyes shining brightly as they stared at him.
"You shouldn’t have barged in like that..."
Nux spoke in a low voice as he pointed at Sharnoth. Shadow, however, just waved her hand, dismissing his words.

After all, she was the Soul of Nux’s Universe, basically the Universe’s Goddess. She knew every single thing that happened in here, so... even trying to hide something from her when she didn’t have absolute authority like Nux did was... somewhat, no, quite foolish.
"Just wake up, will you?
You aren’t fooling anyone."
Shadow spoke, glancing at Sharnoth, but seeing that the woman wasn’t listening and was still continuing with her act, Shadow just sighed as she shook her head.
These amateurs...
"Don’t blame me later,
You brought this upon yourself."
Shadow muttered and at the same time, Allura and the rest of the women walked into the room as well.
However, before they or anyone else in the room could understand what was happening—
"Haaaahhh..."
Shadow took a deep breath in and then—

"lord why is my body still tingling like this every inch of me remembers him inside me filling me stretching me owning me and I don’t want it to stop I can’t let him go if I open my eyes he’ll smile that wicked smile and return to his wives then go fight the infinities and who knows how long before he comes back to me but no no no I need him here with me his warmth his breath on my neck his hands pinning me down again please nux don’t leave me I pretend to sleep but my heart is racing so loud he must hear it feel it through our connection that pull that makes me ache for more I want him to roll over right now grab my wrists like before and thrust into me slow at first teasing until I beg then harder faster making me scream his name again and again until I can’t think anymore—"

She began, saying words so quickly that no mortal would understand any of it. Unfortunately, no being present in the room was a mortal, so every single one of them could understand everything clearly.
The worst part?
Shadow didn’t seem to have any intentions of stopping.
"just feel him pounding claiming every part of me my skin marked with his bites my horns tingling from his fingers tracing them my crimson fol—"
"STOP! STOP!!
WHAT ARE YOU DOING!?"

And within just a few seconds, Sharnoth shot up, sitting on the bed, her crimson eyes glaring at Shadow as an unlimited amount of Chaos Energy gathered around her, as if ready to attack Shadow if she didn’t stop.
But Shadow...
She just stared at Sharnoth’s face, then she looked down and—
"Toot twooott."
She whistled, ogling at her body without shame. Then, she glanced at Nux and—
"No wonder you took your time. Even I feel like giving them a—mmphhhh!!!"
Before the woman could even complete, a shadow formed right beside her and grabbed her mouth, stopping her from speaking anymore.
Yes, it was Lane.
The Shadow Demon also glared at Sharnoth and—
"Cover yourself, will you?"
She spoke and Sharnoth...
She finally realized what had just happened and quickly covered herself with the blanket as her entire face turned red.
"W-What are all of you doing here?"
She asked with a stutter.
[What else? Your turn is over and it’s mine now, so I came to take what’s mine. The rest are here for fun, I think.]
Shadow’s voice echoed throughout the room.
Lane, who was grabbing her mouth, felt her lips twitch in annoyance. To think... to think this woman would use her Authority over the Universe to make the sound move according to her will.
And Shadow...
She looked at Lane with a pitiful look on her face.
[I am sorry, okay? I didn’t say what you didn’t want me to say, now did I? Trust me, no one here will know you are a perv—Aaaahhhh!!!]
Lane’s brown eyes got darker as she gathered her strength in order to crush Shadow’s face into pieces.
Yes, she was prepared to kill her.
But in the end—
"Alright, that’s enough."
Nux spoke up, appearing right beside the two and hugging them gently. Instantly, Lane’s grip loosened. Shadow too, stopped playing around and enjoyed Nux’s hug instead and Sharnoth...
She just stared at the group in front of her with a confused and somewhat... fearful look on her face.
The Chaos Energy she had gathered around her dispersed too. She obviously knew better than to hurt these women.
She knew how much Nux loved them and the last thing she wanted was to hurt him.
But...
As much as she wanted to believe that, the way these women were looking at her... as if she were a sheep sacrificed to these demons...
It... it made her uncomfortable.
Until suddenly—
"Sister Sharnoth~"
She heard a voice and the auburn-haired girl with a cute smile walked towards her with her hands behind her back and a big smile on her face.
"S-Sister...?"
Sharnoth stuttered at those words. Skyla, however, just tilted her head.
"Hmm? Didn’t I always call you Sister? Why do you seem more surprised today? What are you thinking, Sister Sharnoth?"
And in an instant—
Sharnoth’s face turned red.
"N-Nothing in particular. I-I am just surprised by a-all of your s-sudden arrival."
The Chaos Heir stuttered and seeing her like this, Allura’s purple eyes shined even more brightly and she turned towards Nux.
’You and Shadow should leave now.
Leave this place for us.’

"just feel him pounding claiming every part of me my skin marked with his bites my horns tingling from his fingers tracing them my crimson fol—"
"STOP!
STOP!!
WHAT ARE YOU DOING!?"

And within just a few seconds, Sharnoth shot up, sitting on the bed, her crimson eyes glaring at Shadow as an unlimited amount of Chaos Energy gathered around her, as if ready to attack Shadow if she didn’t stop.
But Shadow...
She just stared at Sharnoth’s face, then she looked down and—
"Toot twooott."
She whistled, ogling at her body without shame.
Then, she glanced at Nux and—
"No wonder you took your time.
Even I feel like giving them a—mmphhhh!!!"
Before the woman could even complete, a shadow formed right beside her and grabbed her mouth, stopping her from speaking anymore.
Yes, it was Lane.
The Shadow Demon also glared at Sharnoth and—
"Cover yourself, will you?"
She spoke and Sharnoth...
She finally realized what had just happened and quickly covered herself with the blanket as her entire face turned red.
"W-What are all of you doing here?"
She asked with a stutter.
[What else?
Your turn is over and it’s mine now, so I came to take what’s mine.
The rest are here for fun, I think.]
Shadow’s voice echoed throughout the room.
Lane, who was grabbing her mouth, felt her lips twitch in annoyance.
To think... to think this woman would use her Authority over the Universe to make the sound move according to her will.
And Shadow...
She looked at Lane with a pitiful look on her face.
[I am sorry, okay?
I didn’t say what you didn’t want me to say, now did I?
Trust me, no one here will know you are a perv—Aaaahhhh!!!]
Lane’s brown eyes got darker as she gathered her strength in order to crush Shadow’s face into pieces.
Yes, she was prepared to kill her.
But in the end—
"Alright, that’s enough."
Nux spoke up, appearing right beside the two and hugging them gently.
Instantly, Lane’s grip loosened.
Shadow too, stopped playing around and enjoyed Nux’s hug instead and Sharnoth...
She just stared at the group in front of her with a confused and somewhat... fearful look on her face.
The Chaos Energy she had gathered around her dispersed too.
She obviously knew better than to hurt these women.
She knew how much Nux loved them and the last thing she wanted was to hurt him.
But...
As much as she wanted to believe that, the way these women were looking at her... as if she were a sheep sacrificed to these demons...
It... it made her uncomfortable.
Until suddenly—
"Sister Sharnoth~"
She heard a voice and the auburn-haired girl with a cute smile walked towards her with her hands behind her back and a big smile on her face.
"S-Sister...?"
Sharnoth stuttered at those words.
Skyla, however, just tilted her head.
"Hmm?
Didn’t I always call you Sister?
Why do you seem more surprised today?
What are you thinking, Sister Sharnoth?"
And in an instant—
Sharnoth’s face turned red.
"N-Nothing in particular.
I-I am just surprised by a-all of your s-sudden arrival."
The Chaos Heir stuttered and seeing her like this, Allura’s purple eyes shined even more brightly and she turned towards Nux.
’You and Shadow should leave now.
Leave this place for us.’

chapters.title: Chapter 2228: You are coming with me.
paragraphs: ’You and Shadow should leave now.
Leave this place for us.’
Allura transmitted her thought into Nux’s head, making sure only he heard her.
When he heard her voice, Nux raised his eyebrow, he then turned towards her and seeing her staring at him with those purple eyes shining in amusement, he...
He pouted.
’Are you kicking your husband out...?’
He answered, teary-eyed.
The Succubus rolled her eyes at those words; she obviously wasn’t going to fall for such trickery after so many centuries of being together with this man.
Instead, she was going to use it to her advantage.
’Of course not, I would rather my husband stay with me all the time. I, in fact, have something to tell you in private, how about we go...talkin private?’
She offered, knowing exactly what she was trying to do.
Nux chuckled at those words; obviously, he too knew what Allura was trying to do, but before he could answer—
"Alright! That is it!"
Shadow raised her voice.
Then, she wrapped her body around Nux’s arm tightly and looked right into his eyes with a strong, possessive look on her face.
"You are coming withme.
It is my turn now."
Nux blinked at those words, Allura too narrowed her eyes.
The Succubus didn’t need to think too much; for Shadow to suddenly react so strongly, it meant she had heard their conversation.
Something that shouldn’t have happened since she was directly talking to Nux unless...
"Alright, now come with me!"
Saying those words, Shadow pulled Nux away, and just before she left the door, she glanced at Allura one last time, and the Succubus... she just stared at her in silence, not saying anything else.
Soon, the woman then turned towards another, far more interesting thing in front of her and—
"Sister Sharnoth~"
She called out.
On the other side, as Shadow pulled Nux out of the room and brought him to the hallway, Nux let it all happen.
It was quite amusing to see the girl pulling him so desperately with all her might.
"Come on!! Would you start moving yourself already!? You’ve had your fun, have you not!?"
Just as he thought that, Shadow raised her voice and this time, Nux could no longer control himself and—
"Pffttt."
He laughed out loud, grabbed Shadow’s hand and pulled her close to him. The sudden action froze Shadow, making her widen her eyes in surprise; she... she did not expect it.
"What is it? Were you not able to read that I was planning to do it?"
Nux whispered into her ears in a sensual voice, a voice that sent shivers down Shadow’s entire body.

Nux didn’t miss the opportunity either and pulled her even closer, his hands wrapping around her tightly, one of them quickly moving toward her butt, giving it a firm hold as he pressed it to his body.
Shadow stuttered, not sure what she should say, her mind had spaced out and she wasn’t able to properly form her thoughts.
And Nux—
"I told you this before, did I not?
Stop reading everyone’s minds just because you now can."
Shadow buried her head into Nux’s chest with a guilty look on her face.
"Why did you tease Sharnoth like that?"
Nux asked. Even though his tone was calm, full of love even, Shadow still felt like she was being scolded and, like an adorable little puppy, she began to rub her head on his chest and—
"...I warned her."
"And you knew better than anyone that she was in no state to hear or understand that warning."
Nux answered.
"She could hear it!"
Shadow raised her voice.
"She just didn’t wish to move, she was even thinking of taking my turn!"
"She didn’t even know about your tur—"
"She didn’t know but she was trying to hoard you all for herself! That isn’t allowed! Especially when it is my turn! Only I can have you all to myself! So I... I needed to show her..."
Shadow lowered her voice by the end.

Nux didn’t know what to say; he wanted to tell her that using her connection and authority to read her sisters’ minds wasn’t good but... the woman looked so absolutely adorable that he couldn’t bring himself to say anything.
Shadow, however, misinterpreted his silence and continued to explain herself even further.
"It wasn’t just her special day, it is my special day too.
It is... my first too..."
She spoke in a low voice.
"Your first?"
Nux raised his eyebrow and muttered in a teasing tone and Shadow pinched his skin.
"It is!"
She shouted.
It was the truth; it would be her body’s first time today, she had been waiting for this day for a long time now.
"And she was trying to hoard it for herself! She had it coming!"
Shadow harrumphed. The woman was not apologetic at all.
Nux laughed at that.
"Then what about Allura, why were you reading her thoughts?"
"She... she was trying to hoard it as well!"
Shadow didn’t give away her advantage but Nux—
"You wouldn’t have known that if you weren’t reading her mind."
He answered calmly and Shadow...
She paused for a moment. Nux raised his eyebrow as he continued to stare at her, waiting for an answer and finally—
"I... I forgot to deactivate the ability..."
"So you were reading everyone’s mind at that moment."
Shadow didn’t say anything, but she didn’t have to. Nux already knew the answer.
"I had more important things in my mind!
I wasn’t interested in any of their thoughts anyway!
I am only interested in you!"
The woman declared proudly, not even a tinge of shame on her face.
At that strong declaration, Nux smiled and in the end—
"Alright alright.
Just don’t make a habit out of it, okay? You know your sisters won’t let you go if they find out that you have been secretly reading their thoughts."
He gave in.
What else was he supposed to do anyway?
He could already tell that this wasn’t a battle he could win; Shadow was simply too adorable for him to be able to counter her words.
"Yes."
Shadow nodded brightly as she once again buried her face into his chest and Nux...
The only thing he could do was pull the woman even closer to him and—
"Then let’s begin your special day, shall we?"
He asked in a soft, seductive voice and unlike Sharnoth, whose entire face would have turned red and body tensed at that statement,
Shadow only hugged him more tightly and—
"YES!!"
She answered excitedly, her voice bright and impatient, her arms squeezing him as if she never wanted to let go.
Nux laughed quietly. He could feel the excitement vibrating through Shadow’s body, the way her heart raced faster than it ever had before.
He could feel all her intense emotions.
Yes, Shadow had a body before but...

In the end, it still wasn’t a ’real’ body; it was something Shadow had materialised just so she could be with him like the others were, but even then, Shadow wasn’t... truly with him because deep down, she knew it as well.
It was all... an illusion.
A temporary happiness.
But now,
Now things were different.
Now, Shadow had a new, real body.
Centuries of waiting, of watching, of seeing others experience what... she wanted to experience...
Now, finally, she too could feel the same.
She could touch his skin and feel him touching her skin, kiss his lips and feel his lips on hers; she now... had a body that could truly feel every inch of him.
And as that thought got stronger in her head, Shadow’s eyes became hazier as she began drowning her mind with... anticipation.
Nux, who could feel all those intense emotions flooding into her mind, gently tilted her chin up with his fingers, meeting those deep purple eyes that shined like twin galaxies.
Her long black hair spilled over his hand, the faint purple gradients at the ends catching the hallway’s soft light.
She looked like the night sky itself had taken human form just for him and right now...
That night sky was full of... desire.
Desire so strong that she wanted nothing more than to devour this man standing in front of her.
Nux chuckled.
"Then let’s begin with a walk, shall we?"
He teased.
Taking such walks with him alone was something Shadow liked quite a bit, so the woman would almost never say no to this offer, but...
Today was one of those exceptions and Nux knew that well.
Shadow too felt her mouth twitch; she could tell Nux was teasing her but she had no intention of giving in to his teasing.
"No. I’ve waited long enough. I don’t want dates or walks.
I want you.
Now.
Take me to my room."
She spoke in a firm, decisive tone, staring at Nux with desire practically flowing out of her eyes.
And Nux...
"Aww, I thought you liked going on walks with me.
So it was only me, huh..."
He pouted and Shadow’s mouth twitched even further as she...
She pulled her husband’s collar, forcefully bringing his face close to hers.

chapters.title: Chapter 2229: Shall we truly begin your special day? *
paragraphs: "Aww, I thought you liked going on walks with me.
So it was only me, huh..."
Nux lowered his head and spoke in a low voice, trying to ’hide his sadness,’ and Shadow...
Her mouth twitched even further and then she pulled her husband’s collar, forcefully bringing his face close to hers.
"Nux Leander."
She called out.
"I have been waiting for this for centuries.
I have been desperate.
My body is burning and my control over myself is at its lowest.
So you better stop playing these games, or trust me when I say this—
This will not end well for you at all."
The woman warned directly, her purple eyes shining so intensely that for a moment, Nux was overwhelmed.
An awkward grin then appeared on his face and—
"Yes, Ma’am."
He nodded like the good husband he was.
Without wasting any time, the space around them folded in a ripple of dark energy with a simple thought.
One moment they were standing in the hallway; the next, they appeared inside Shadow’s private mansion—a palace they had shaped just for Shadow alone.
The mansion floated in an endless void of swirling stars and soft purple mist. Its walls were made of smooth obsidian and living shadow, warm to the touch despite their dark colour.

Crystal chandeliers drifted lazily above, each gem glowing with captured starlight that cast gentle, shifting patterns across the floor. The air carried a faint, sweet scent of midnight flowers that only bloomed in places without true daylight.
The two walked deeper, passing through wide archways and floating staircases, until they reached the bedroom.
The doors parted silently at his approach, revealing a vast room.
The walls here were made of glass, showing slow-moving galaxies turning in silence outside, streaks of violet and silver light painting everything in cool, sensual tones.
Tiny motes of light drifted like fireflies, responding to their presence by gathering closer, as if the room itself was... eager to watch.

And in the very centre was the bed, large enough to hold twenty people and still have space left. It was framed in dark polished wood that seemed to drink in the starlight, draped in layers of black silk so soft that one’s entire body would sink into the bed the moment they lay down.
The sheets and pillows shined faintly as well, made from pure, cool and weightless shadows. Plush cushions in deep purple and midnight blue were scattered across the bed.

The entire mansion, from even the smallest side of the garden to the bedroom, was suited to Shadow’s taste, and as she walked into the familiar room with her new body while pulling Nux by his collar, she stared at her bed with her eyes filled with hunger.
Shadow didn’t speak; she didn’t need to.
The way her eyes were now looking at him was all Nux needed to see to hear and fully understand all her thoughts.
At first, he decided to let Shadow have the control, letting her lead him to the edge, but the next second, as the room’s environment began to affect his mind—
The look in his eyes changed and he—
He contradicted himself.
Yes, he didn’t even last a few seconds before giving into his urges, his hands that had been holding back till now moved.
First, he grabbed her waist in a firm, possessive manner, then in one smooth motion, he turned her, lifted her just enough, and...
He pushed.
"Haah..."
Shadow fell back onto the bed with a soft low gasp, her long hair spreading across the dark silk like spilled ink.

The sheets rippled beneath her in a cool, welcoming manner, moulding perfectly to her body. She looked up at him, a faint blush appearing on her cheeks, her eyes shining with anticipation and... desire.
"Then..."
Nux spoke in a low voice as he stood at the foot of the bed, gazing down at this ridiculously beautiful woman and—
"Shall we truly begin yourspecial day?"
At those words, Shadow’s purple eyes locked onto his, her breath coming in quick, shallow bursts as she lay there on the silken sheets.
Nux hadn’t even done anything yet but... her body had already started to react.

After all, this wasn’t actually her first time. Even though her body was different, Shadow had been together with this man for centuries. The gaze with which he was looking at her right now... it was imprinted into her very mind so strongly that nothing could overpower it.
She knew... she knew what was going to happen next.
Her mind remembered that overwhelming amount of pleasure it was about to be drowned in. This was the reason that even though her new body was clueless as to what it was about to go through...
Unconsciously, as it began picking up the signals her brain was sending, it had begun to react.
And Nux...
As he saw this lovely sight in front of him... he was just... mesmerized.

Shadow’s face was the epitome of perfection—high cheekbones, full lips parted slightly in anticipation, and those eyes, deep amethyst pools that seemed to hold the secrets of the universe itself. Her skin glowed with an ethereal smoothness, untouched and... flawless, as if she were a goddess meant only for distant admiration, not the warmth of mortal touch.

Yet here she was, her body curved in absolute harmony—her generous breasts rising and falling with each breath, a narrow waist flaring into hips that begged to be held, her long and toned legs that wanted to wrap themselves around Nux.
Every inch of her body was an incarnation of beauty so devastating it made Nux’s cheeks warm with a rare blush.
Yes, even Nux—when he saw someone with such an absurdly perfect body lying there with such open desire—was blushing.
Just that thought alone made his little brother twitch, awakening as he sensed the mood.
Slowly, Nux climbed onto the bed, his weight making the sheets shift beneath.
Shadow reached for him boldly, her fingers tracing the lines of his shirt as if she wanted to pull him down faster.
But before she could do what she wanted—Nux caught her wrists and pinned them above her head with one hand.
"Not so fast."
He whispered softly, his other hand sliding down, tracing a line on her soft, precious body.
"Let me savour you first."
He spoke, his seductive voice sending shivers down Shadow’s spine as her mind began imagining things that were not safe for kids at all.
Her body squirmed in reaction, her boldness cracking under his teasing gaze.
Shadow was direct by nature, shameless even. She always asked for what she wanted without hesitation, and that behaviour only grew stronger with time, however, there was a catch.

While the woman was shameless most of the time, when Nux turned the tables like this and took control—when his eyes began to ogle her, when his hands began to move, touching every part of her body in a slow, deliberate manner...
Shadow’s directness... falters.
Just like it was happening right now.
She whispered softly, to the point even Nux could barely hear her.
But that little voice held so many intense emotions—want, desire, half protest, half... plea. Soon, her body betrayed her as well, arching slightly toward him, craving... more.
Nux smiled at that. Then, he leaned down, his lips brushing hers in a soft, almost teasing kiss.
Shadow responded eagerly, her mouth opening to him. Once again, she somehow regained her boldness and her tongue took charge.
"Ugghmmhh~"
Moving into his mouth with a hunger that made even Nux groan. Yes, Shadow now held the advantage, or at least, that was what she thought as she thought about moving even more intensely but then—
Nux pulled back.
And no, he didn’t move all the way back to break the kiss; he moved just enough to... make her chase him, and that is what Shadow did.
She moved, chasing him exactly how he wanted her to, but Nux—
His lips curved into that familiar, sadistic grin, and his free hand slid to her jaw, stopping her from getting close.
Shadow frowned, but Nux tilted her head to expose the elegant line of her neck.
"Look at you,"
He breathed against her skin. His hot breath sent even stronger shivers through her body, making it weaker and... tamer.
"So... perfect."
Nux praised. His voice was like an aphrodisiac that turned on every part of Shadow’s body but...
Shadow wasn’t the only one who seemed like she was affected by an aphrodisiac. Nux was affected by one as well.
And his was... different.
His was... more permanent.
"Every curve, every inch...
It’s like you were made to drive me mad."
He spoke, his voice cracking as he controlled his desire and held back his urges. Just like her, he too wanted nothing more than to tear her clothes and devour her right then and there, but...
At the same time—
He wanted to savour her too.
He wanted to enjoy every part of her body and take as much time as he wanted. He wanted to make this...
Unforgettable, for both of them.
Slowly, his lips pressed on her neck’s pulse point, feeling it race under his touch.
"Haahh..."
Shadow gasped, her fists clenching the bedsheets tightly as her entire body jerked in pleasure.
And Nux—
He suddenly lifted his head and paused. His eyebrow rising as he realized something—something that even Shadow didn’t seem to know yet.
