Nux!!
Nux!
Don’t leave me!
Hard—"
"STOP!!
STOP!!!
WHAT ARE YOU DOING!?"
Once again, Sharnoth screamed, her face now completely flushed, and Allura could swear she could see smoke coming out of her head.
"Oh?
Do you recall it now?
Or do I..."
Allura asked, not needing to complete her words.
I do..."
Sharnoth lowered her head, trying to hide her face.
For the first time in her entire life she felt... so pressured by someone weaker than her.
"So you do."
Allura smiled.
Then she walked forward and sat on the bed right in front of her.
"Then what do you remember, Sister?
Mind sharing the details?"
The succubus asked, her grin becoming so wide that Skyla and Evane actually began feeling bad for Sharnoth.
I don’t..."
Sharnoth didn’t know how to respond but then—
"Sister Sharnoth, it’s alright, you don’t have to.
Sister Allura is just teasing you."
Skyla spoke up as she appeared next to her new sister and glared at the older one.
Allura glanced at Skyla and raised her eyebrow, not liking how her fun was ruined.
But then—
"Teasing me...?"
Sharnoth tilted her head, confused.
"Yes, she does it with everyone once they become a Leander, so don’t think too much."
"Become a Leander...?"
At those words, Sharnoth frowned even more strongly—a reaction the women did not fail to notice.
Well, everyone except for Skyla, that is.
"Yes, after you—mmhhfff!!"
The innocent maid tried to answer but suddenly, Thyra appeared behind her and grabbed her mouth.

Rune didn’t waste time either and quickly grabbed the maid’s hands, stopping her from resisting too much, and Melia took the chance to put the three of them inside a Blood Dome, separate from Sharnoth.
"Wha—?"
Everything happened so quickly that Sharnoth couldn’t even react in time.
Of course, at her level, her reaction speed should be much higher than these women’s but... her body was currently in a resting stage.
After all, all her piled-up stress, her worries, her inhibitions... they were all forced out of her body and replaced by something... far, far more... addicting.
A pleasure she had never experienced in her long, long life.
Obviously her body and her mind were in no state to react to things happening around her.
Not to mention this was Nux’s Universe—a place she knew for a fact was safe for her—so she too had let her guard down, even though she was currently intimidated by all these women around her.
"Don’t worry about her."
Suddenly, Amaya spoke up, walking up to Sharnoth with a gentle smile on her face—a smile that made Sharnoth frown.
This entire situation felt suspicious.
Very, very suspicious.
This wasn’t her first time interacting with these women.
Ever since she came here, she had interacted with them quite a few times.
Some of these women stared at her as if she were a challenge—someone they wanted to defeat in a battle—but since they weren’t currently at the same level, they were waiting.

Some women actively discussed plans, strategies, and things they could do to help Nux—a discussion she liked to participate in since she had a huge pile of debt she needed to repay to Nux, and helping him this way was the least she could do.
Some women, especially this succubus in front of her, always talked to her strangely, like she had something in her mind when she looked at her, but she never said it out loud.
And some... like Amaya—
Always stared at her with a look of disapproval.

As if she wanted nothing more than for her to leave—something she could just not do since she had already promised herself to Nux and was prepared to serve him for the rest of her life in...anyway possible.
But today... something felt different.
No, it wasn’t different.
It was... eerie.
To think the woman who always had that look of disapproval now had a smile on her face...
Something was definitely wrong here.
She just did not know what it was.
For now, however, Sharnoth just smiled back.
After all, no matter how she looked at her, this woman was Nux’s wife—one of the few people Nux cherished more than his own life.
She couldn’t be rude to her just because she looked at her funny.
"Did you enjoy it...?"
Suddenly, Amaya asked, the gentle smile on her face still not fading.
"What are you..."
Sharnoth tried to ask but—
"You know what I am talking about.
We are all grown-ups here, let’s not waste our time with these games, okay?
And I am not asking you for any details, now am I?
I just want to know if you had fun."
Amaya interrupted with a light smile.
When she excused the details, Aisha tried to interrupt but one look from Amaya was more than enough to stop her.
After all, Aisha understood it as well—this was more important than some details.
This... would benefit them all in the long run.
"I-I enjoyed it."
Sharnoth nodded.
"So you do not feel bad at all, huh?"
Amaya pressed, and Sharnoth—
She lowered her head even further.
"A-All of you were busy, and Nux came to me.
I had promised myself to him so I could not reject him."
The Chaos Heir answered, and the moment she did, Amaya’s eyes shined.
And not just hers—the rest of the women were the same.
Some even exchanged light smiles, smiles even Sharnoth did not catch.
The Chaos Heir was just too confused to understand anything, as for the women—
They understood it.
Either Nux hadn’t asked her about it or Sharnoth had forgotten about it.
The woman still believed that instead of becoming part of Nux’s family, she was just... a subordinate—someone below them in the ’hierarchy.’
If they played their cards right...
They might be able to get... a few more ’turns’ out of this.
"So that is to say, as long as any one of us is free, you would step back, correct?"
"I-If Nux wants me then..."
Sharnoth answered with a stutter, and Amaya raised her eyebrow even further—
"What did you say?"
"I meant... i-it is Nux’s decision... i-if he comes to me, then as someone who has promised herself to him, I cannot reject him, I...
I will not go against my words."
"Right."
Amaya nodded.
"So as long as Nux doesn’t come to you himself, you will stay put, is that right?"
Sharnoth didn’t say anything, but Amaya did not stop.
"What?
That is what you meant to say, correct?
The devourer then narrowed her eyes as she walked even closer, standing right on top of the Chaos Heir—
"Or do you have... some other ideas in your mind?"
"N-No.
I-I do not."
Sharnoth lowered her head and nodded.
Even if she wanted to go against this woman and push her away, she was Nux’s wife.
There was nothing she could do.
"Good."
Amaya nodded, satisfied.

"So I can assume that when Nux gives you a ’turn’ to spend time with him, if any of us wishes, we can come to you and take your turn to spend time with him as long as Nux wishes to spend time with us, yes?"
She asked one last time, making sure everything was clear, and Sharnoth—she...
She didn’t know why...
But she felt like if she said yes to that question, she would regret it for the rest of her life, so instead—
"Heh."
She grinned.
"To think there will be a day when weaklings like you would dare to surround and bully... me.
Oh, how low have I fallen~"
Sharnoth let her other self take over.

chapters.title: Chapter 2235: Aren’t you glad you all followed me here?
paragraphs: "Heh."
Suddenly, Sharnoth grinned.

Making the rest of the women around her frown in confusion, the Chaos Heir, however, did not care—her grin only widened even further to the point her face distorted and cracks began to appear on her facial skin and—
"To think there will be a day when weaklings like you would dare to surround and bully... me.
Oh, how low have I fallen~"
She spoke as she stared at the women around her, her crimson eyes flaring strongly, and the instant the women saw her reaction, they understood it.
’Normal’ Sharnoth was no longer with them—
She had let the ’crazy one’ take over.
"I must make things right, shouldn’t I?"

Sharnoth spoke, her grin stretching even wider as she began measuring the women. For a moment, the women too felt intimidated by her gaze. After all, they knew how strong Sharnoth was, and while the ’normal Sharnoth’ still had control over herself... this one was...
Anything could happen.
But...
As soon as that thought appeared in their heads, it disappeared.
This was about Nux. There was no way they would get intimidated here.
"Set things right? And how do you plan on doing that?"
Aeliana asked, her crimson eyes beginning to shine as well.
"How else? I will teach all of you your place."
Sharnoth answered, her eyes glowing even stronger.
This... this was fun.
After all, in her mind, she knew about the connection. She knew these women could not be killed as long as they were in this Universe, and that meant...
They were toys who wouldn’t break anytime soon.
But...
"Teach us... our place...?"
Things weren’t as easy as Sharnoth was expecting, especially when she was dealing with women just as crazy as her—if not more.
"You...are going to show us...ourplace?"
Vyriana raised an eyebrow, but Sharnoth just tilted her head.
"Why not?
You wanted to face me anyway, did you not?
I am giving you the chance now. Or are you too scared?"
The Chaos Heir taunted the Dragon, but before the Dragon could give in to the taunt and participate in the Eternal’s game—
"Are you suggesting that you are going to use your strength to suppress us?"
Amaya raised her eyebrow, and in an instant, Sharnoth jumped at those words.
"Don’t be naïve, girl."
She answered.
"The entire Universe revolves around strength. I lost what I cherished because I was weak. You..."
Her crimson eyes then darkened and—
"You should try experiencing the same."
Saying those words, Sharnoth stood up. Her physical body felt strange and weak for some reason, so she began shedding her skin to abandon her body.
Yes, this was no longer just a mere... joke.
It was going to turn into a full-grown confrontation—
Or at least... that was what Sharnoth thought.
"Take this as a lesson,
A lesson that teaches you your place, a lesson that...
You shouldn’t stand up to and surround your betters just because you have numbers, because even a horde do—"
Before Sharnoth could even complete her words—
"So I am right to assume that strength and means define the results, correct?"
Amaya asked calmly.
"Yes, you have learned well, but don’t think this—"
Sharnoth answered with a grin. She didn’t seem in any particular hurry since she wanted to enjoy it but—
"So as long as we make it so Nux never sees you again, you won’t find it unfair and will accept your defeat, yes?"
"Hah?"
Sharnoth paused, then she laughed.
"As if you can—"
"Just answer my question."
Amaya interrupted with a light smile. Sharnoth momentarily frowned.
This...
This wasn’t fun at all.
The woman was asking too many questions! It annoyed her!
BUT—
Sharnoth also knew that the more arrogant the enemy, the more... joyful it is to crush them. Seeing this arrogant woman’s fall would be quite fun indeed~
With that thought in her mind—
"Yes—"
The Chaos Heir tried to answer but then—
"Don’t be foolish."
She herself changed her answer as the cracks on her face began to recover. This, however, did not last long. Her eyes, that had just lost their light, intensified again and—
"What are you doing?"
Sharnoth asked out loud, and once again, the cracks began to heal and her frown disappeared.
"They are his wives. Hurting them would hurt hi—"
"I am only teaching them a lesso—"
"You have no right to do tha—"
"I have every right to do whatever I want because I am stro—"
Sharnoth began talking... in a strange manner. To others, it would seem she had lost her mind, but the women could see it.
This was the ’normal Sharnoth’ and ’crazy Sharnoth’ fighting with each other, forcefully taking over the body and interrupting the other.

Whenever ’normal Sharnoth’ took over, her voice became calmer and the cracks on her face started to heal, but as soon as the crazy one took over, the voice became heavier, the cracks began to widen, and the eyes... they shone more intensely.
This continued, the two personalities going at each other, but then—
"Not stronger than me."
The ’normal Sharnoth’ replied, and for an instant—
Sharnoth did not speak, but the rest of the women could sense the tension in the air rising.
This time, as the crazy Sharnoth took over, she did not smile. Neither did the skin crack. Instead—
In a much heavier voice than before—
"What...?"
She asked, as she once again let the normal Sharnoth take over.
"I said, you are not stronger than me."
Normal Sharnoth did not back down either.
"And what gave you that confidence?"
Crazy Sharnoth laughed as she then raised her voice.
"I am the one who fights our battles because I am the stronger one. How is that hard to und—"
"You are stronger when you fight other opponents, but in the battle between the two of us...
You cannot win."
Normal Sharnoth answered calmly.
"In what world..."
Crazy Sharnoth couldn’t believe what she was hearing.
"If the two of us fought, you would los—"
She tried to answer, but once again—
"I ’would’ lose if we faced each other in two different bodies, but that cannot happen. As long as we share the same body, I can take over whenever I desire—just like you.
You can never win unless you find a way to make me disappear—permanently."
Normal Sharnoth answered, and finally, the crazy one began to realize it.
"...Why are you doing this?"
She asked.
"I am fighting for us."
"This is not a fight."
Normal Sharnoth answered. She then turned towards the women and—
"They are not our enemies."
"They tried to suppress you."
"They do not have totry.Nux is their husband. They have all the right over him—more than I can ever have on hi—"
"But you can just take him away after you defeat them al—"
"No."
Normal Sharnoth shook her head. Then, her gaze hardened and—
"You should leave now. You said you only wanted to appear during a fight or when Vexarion’s around.
Nothing’s happening yet.
As for my ’turn’..."
Normal Sharnoth glanced at the women and—
"I will let them decide how they want i—"
"Wait."
Before normal Sharnoth could complete, the crazy one raised her voice one last time.
"Yourturn...?"
She narrowed her eyes, and the normal Sharnoth—
She blinked in surprise.
"Ourturn."
Crazy Sharnoth corrected, but normal Sharnoth stood strong.
"What are you talking about? This is not about sparring with Nux. You can enjoy that all for yourself. This is not a figh—"
"He attacked you again and again, sending those strange shivers throughout your body that weakened you—
Itwasa fight.
Look at our body’s state after you lost. You cannot even stand properly!
So from now on, I will fight instead."
Crazy Sharnoth declared, but in an instant—
"Don’t be absurd!"
Normal Sharnoth raised her voice. This time, her eyes flared much more strongly and—
"Do not go back on your words by twisting the facts! This is not a battle!"
"I am not twisting my words! You were attacked and you do not even realize it!"
"Have you lost your min—"
"You have lost your mind!!"
"No you—"

As the ’fight’ between the two intensified, the rest of the women present here... they just stared at her in silence, unable to process what was happening to the woman, even though they knew exactly what the problem was.
And of course, even though they knew the solution, none of them said it out loud. That would be foolish.
They had come here to gain, not to lose.
Instead,
The women just sat in silence, observing everything that was happening with amused looks on their faces—especially Allura.
The succubus turned towards the rest of her sisters, her purple eyes shining brightly in strong amusement.
"See? I told you this would be fun, didn’t I?
Aren’t you glad you all followed me here?"
She obviously did not expectthiswhen she came here, but she was definitely enjoying this.

chapters.title: Chapter 2236: Explain it in clear details.
paragraphs: "Alright then—"
After a long, long discussion, the crazy Sharnoth finally sighed, lowering her voice for the first time in a while.
"Yes, it is decided then."
Normal Sharnoth nodded too. The Crazy Sharnoth once again took over the body and turned towards the rest of the women—
"We will both have our separate turns."
She announced.
And the women who were watching the show...
They blinked at the absurdity of those words.
"And you think we would just... let it happen?"
Amaya raised her eyebrow.
What gave these two that idea?
Was she not being yandere enough?
Did she not make her intentions clear enough?
Was she... lacking?
It wasn’t just her; the rest of the women were the same. What gave the idea that they were too easygoing?
This was especially true when the troublesome element like Skyla was already taken away.
"What? You have a problem with that?"
The Crazy Sharnoth raised her voice again, her crimson eyes shining more intensely, but in the next second, her eyes lost their shine and—
"Let me do the talking."
She spoke in a calmer voice as normal Sharnoth took over.
"Are you sure?"
The crazy Sharnoth asked.
"Yes, do not forget the rule—you do the fighting, I do the talking."
Sharnoth replied, and this time, the crazy one did not take over.
It was clear that she had agreed. Finally, Sharnoth—who had constantly been shifting between two different personalities every single second—became... calmer.
The woman then stared at the rest of the women around her and—
"I... apologize for everything that happened."
She spoke as she bowed lightly.
"I couldn’t care less about that little show; no need to apologize for it. What youdoneed to explain is what was said at the very end."
Amaya took the lead in the conversation. The devourer stepped closer to the Chaos Heir and—
"We come here to confront you about what you have done with our husband, and instead of apologizing, you talk about wanting separate ’turns’ for your two personalities?
Do you... not put us in your eyes at all...?"
The devourer narrowed her eyes.
"I-It isn’t like that..."
Sharnoth didn’t know what to say.

"I did not thinkshewould... want her turn. My memories of those times are hazy, but that isn’t the case for her. She remembers every single detail as clearly as if it happened yesterday. She still feels the same emotions she felt those days and, together with all those other emotions...
She...
She also carries the same... fear of the act."
Sharnoth began to explain in an awkward tone; it felt quite strange to talk about... her other self like this.

"Never once in my life do I remember her getting over that fear. Even when Nux got close to me, I could sense her trembling inside me, not willing to come out. I never expected her to... fight so hard regarding this matter and show interest like this."
For a moment, the women turned silent at those words—Amaya too. She wanted to say this wasn’t her problem, but... even she didn’t go that far.
After all, in her mind, she already knew this woman was one of her sisters; she was only here to scam a few turns out of her, not actually isolate her from the rest.
That was not how family worked.
But then—
"If she’s interested, why not give her your turns?"
Allura asked with a playful look on her face, and Sharnoth—the Chaos Heir—once again looked away, unable to say it.
Of course, the Succubus wasn’t letting this go.
This was the entire reason she had come here to begin with~
"Hmmmmmmm?"
The Succubus tilted her head as she moved closer.
"Why won’t you answer?"
She asked innocently, moving her face right in front of Sharnoth’s, making sure she doesn’t get to ’look away.’
And Sharnoth...
She couldn’t reply. Under the succubus’s pressure, her face turned red, but even then, she couldn’t respond.
It was too embarrassing.
Allura’s purple eyes shined in amusement, then suddenly, another succubus appeared right beside the two of them, moving her mouth close to Sharnoth’s ear and—
"You know it will be far easier if you admit it, don’t you?"

Aisha whispered into Sharnoth’s ear like a demon trying to tempt a helpless mortal. Sharnoth’s body froze; Aisha, on the other hand, looked at Allura, their purple eyes now shining together as the two smiled at each other and then—
"Everything you have been holding back, let it out."
"Accept the truth,
Saythe truth."
"Be free."
"Understand your desires."
"Act on your desires."
"This is the only chance you have."
"If you do not make the proper move here—"
"These women will take away what you now cherish the most."
"Permanently."
The two succubi spoke without stopping, one after another, whispering words of... ’wisdom’ into Sharnoth’s head, and the more she heard them—
The more Sharnoth felt like her mind was freezing.

As the two women surrounded her, whispering all these words into her head...
She...
She couldn’t think of her reply.
"Think about it."
Aisha spoke again.
"Everything you felt."
Allura added.
"Every touch."
Aisha spoke.
"Every jolt of pleasure that coursed through your body."
Allura whispered.
"Every time your body flinched and squelched for more."
"Every time you... throbbed."
"Think about it all."
"Think about everything Nux did to you."
"Think about everything Nuxwoulddo to you in future."
"Do you... not want that?"
"Are you... not going to fight for what you... enjoyed so much?"
"Can you... live without it?"
The women continued their song of whispers and temptation, making Sharnoth’s face even redder.

In their minds, the women were blaming the succubus mother.
And they weren’t wrong either.
One of these two women was the ’product’ she gave birth to, and the other... she was the one who turned her into a succubus.
So yes, Eisheth was to blame, and the Succubus mother...
She just blinked at those stares, not knowing how to react to them.

"I don’t want to!"
Sharnoth muttered in a voice so low that because of Allura’s and Aisha’s constant whispers, the women couldn’t hear it.
The Chaos Heir’s face right now was completely flushed, her body had curled up, her eyes were closed, as if she no longer wanted to watch what was happening around her.
The strongest woman in the room—an Eternal, in fact probably one of the strongest Eternals in the main Universe—looked like a scared and nervous prey surrounded by a bunch of predators.
"What did you say?"
Allura asked, her eyes gleaming even more strongly.

Allura asked.
"Do you truly wish to give up on your desires?"
Aisha whispered.
"Even if your mind somehow forgets, can your body forge—"
"I said I don’t want to!"

"What is it that you do not want?"

"I do not wish to share my ’turns’ with her!"

"And why is that?"
This time, Edda finally found an opening and joined in.
"Because I want Nux."
Sharnoth answered.
"I want him to do everything he did to me—
Every. Single. Day."
"Oh? So you liked it that much, eh?"
Edda asked, walking closer and sitting on the bed.
"Yes."
And Sharnoth nodded.
"So what exactly did he do to you that you liked so much?"
Edda asked another question, and while normally Sharnoth in her right mind would never answer that question—
Right now, the woman had lost her filters,
"Everything.
I liked everything he did to me."
"And whatisthiseverything?"
Allura asked again. Aisha too moved a little and began her little whispers.
"Explain it in clear details,
From the beginning to the end.
Relive that moment with your words, feel everything you felt back then,
Come on,
Let go of the restraints—
Unleash your desires."
The Succubus spoke and Sharnoth—
"He first brought me here and ordered me to his pillow..."
The Chaos Heir began her story, and the rest of the women, they too jumped onto the bed, listening with great curiosity.

"Are you sure?"

"Yes, do not forget the rule—you do the fighting, I do the talking."

chapters.title: Chapter 2237: Escape.
paragraphs: Silence.
Absolute silence.
That was the first thing Vexarion Aurendor noticed after he got... far enough.
It was... strange.
Yes, the silence itself was strange. It was different from the silence inside an empty room; it was... the silence of a place that... never learned to speak.
There were no familiar currents in the air. No old ’echoes’ left behind by ancient cultivators. No distant pulses from high-level worlds. No faint traces of other Eternals moving somewhere far away.
There was just... space.
Vast, dark space... and worlds that felt young.
And that thought alone made his chest tighten.
A place like this should not exist.
Vexarion Aurendor was an Eternal. A being who had been in this Universe for more than a million years, a being who had alliances, enemies, and debts scattered across every corner of creation.
There were very few regions he hadn’t visited himself—at the very least, he had heard of them.
But this?
This was unfamiliar in a way that felt... wrong.
Still, his mind refused to accept the worst conclusion.
It didn’t even allow it.
Because the worst conclusion required a thought his mind could not comprehend.
Another Universe?
No.
That was nonsense.
That was... madness.
So he forced his thoughts into something he could hold.
The Universe expands constantly, without stopping.
It was the oldest truth of existence.
Worlds are born. Planes are formed. Stars gather. Order takes shape. Empty regions... fill up.
And sometimes—sometimes—new parts of the Universe appeared so recently that the living hadn’t mapped them yet.
Yes, exactly.
This must be a part of the Universe that was formed recently, a part that hadn’t been explored yet.
That explanation was... imperfect.
But it was still... an explanation.
And right now, Vexarion needed one.
Because if this was still the Universe he belonged to...
Then it meant there was still a way out.
He could return.
Hewouldreturn.
With determination in his eyes, he stared ahead, his black wings spread wide, golden veins glowing under his obsidian skin, and he flapped his wings, increasing his speed even further.
After all, slowing down wasn’t an option. Not even when his ribs ached from pushing speed beyond what was comfortable, nor when his entire body screamed to rest.
Because the moment he slowed down—
He remembered.
That grey sky.
That empty land.
That laugh that... did not stop.
That grin that widened even when his body was torn apart.
And...
And that pain.
Pain that had no end.
Pain that did not kill him to release him, but killed him just to bring him back again and again and... again.
Vexarion remembered everything: the sound of his halo cracking, his heart being crushed, the moment his mind simply shut off because... it just couldn’t hold out anymore.
His entire body flinched when he recalled that time.
"No."
He whispered in a hoarse, unfamiliar voice. His own voice felt foreign to him, as if he hadn’t spoken for decades.
And even now, his mind was somewhat confused; he didn’t know who he was speaking to.
Maybe it was... himself.
Or the Universe.
Or maybe it was the empty darkness around him.
He did not know, but he continued.
"No. Not again."
He spoke, and with his intent now clearer when he said it out loud, he continued flying.
He flew until the strange region swallowed the memory of that grey land, until his breath became steady again, until the fear... stopped choking him.
And then—
He began tohope.
At first, hope came easily.
It came like an old habit.
He was an Eternal of Light’s faction. He had survived wars that had turned galaxies into ash. He had been trapped, cornered, and challenged before.
But...
He had neverstayedtrapped.
He had never stayed... helpless.
And now he had something he did not have in that nightmare.
Distance.
Space.
And...
Time.
He could now think.
He could now plan.
He could now... move.

Without waiting, he looked through his personal dimension and took out all the call artifacts. Some of these were made for emergencies. Some for secrecy. Some were made for direct links to specific allies.
He activated the first, hoping for it to work now that he was away, but...
Nothing.
There was no pulse, no flicker, and no... reply.
But he did not give up.
He activated the second.
But again, nothing happened.
He then took the third.
The fourth.
Fifth, sixth, seventh...
Even the one Auren gave him—an artifact meant to work even under heavy restriction, even across sealed zones.
He poured energy into it until the golden veins on his arms flared, but...
The artifact stayed dead.
Vexarion’s brows tightened.
The memory of the artifact exploding in Sharnoth’s presence flashed in his mind, and his fingers trembled for a moment.
He forcefully steadied his mind and—
"It’s fine,"
he muttered to himself.
"This region is new.
The laws here must be... unstable.
This is why they aren’t working."
This was the explanation his mind had come up with. This region was newly formed; the Universe here was... still settling into itself.
Even time itself was somewhat strange here. It was moving—of course it was; it allowed him to think, breathe, he could even count moments and sense the flow of time—but...
The flow of time was... different from how it... should be.
Sometimes it felt like hours passed too quickly.
Sometimes it felt like his thoughts stretched too long, like a single breath carried too much space between start and end.
He couldn’t explain it.
He tried to measure it by stars.
But even the stars here were strange.
They were not arranged like the constellations he knew. They didn’t carry the same ancient patterns that most of the Universe shared.
He tried to measure it by his own body.
But his body was still recovering from what his mind had endured. His senses were sharp, but his emotions were... uneven.
So he shrugged and blamed it on the same thing.
A new region.
A... young region that was not completed yet.
That would explain the strange time flow.
That would explain the dead artifacts.
That would explain why the worlds he found felt half-formed.
And he did find worlds.
He found them after the first ’day’ he escaped.
And no, the ’day’ he mentioned wasn’t like what mortals believed, with sunrise and sunset, but a span of time he chose to count as a day because he needed structure.
So on the first ’day’, he found a world—a small planet drifting alone in the dark, wrapped in thin clouds.
He landed on it carefully, wings folding behind him as his feet touched soil.
The soil was... cold. Not frozen—just cold, like it hadn’t known warmth for long.

He looked around. The sky was pale grey, the atmosphere was weak. There were plants, simple ones, moss that clung to rocks. Low ferns that trembled when wind passed, small... strange insects crawling in lines.
Beasts, too—small, skittish creatures with thin bodies and wide eyes, running the moment they sensed him.
There were no cities, no roads, no carved stone, no towers, no traces of cultivators, no... overly complicated life.
All the ’living’ he sensed here were creatures that did not have a mind of their own; they only existed because... they should. They could not cultivate, they could not even think, let alone talk.
Vexarion walked through that world for hours, scanning with his senses. He found a lake, a mountain, a forest that looked like it had only existed for a short time.
But... he found no mind that could speak.
It was clear.
This world hadn’t given birth to intelligent lifeforms yet.
But...
He tried anyway.
"Is anyone here?"
He stood in the center of the forest and let his voice spread.
The words rolled across the trees and... died.
He tried a different method.
He released a wave of divine pressure to make living things react, and they did—the insects scattered, the beasts fled, the plants shook, but...
That was all.
Vexarion stared at the empty air and exhaled slowly.
"Nothing, huh..."
He paused, finally accepting the truth.
"Fine,"
He whispered.
"Not here."
With those words, he left and...
He flew again.
Then, he found another world.
This one had oceans.
Huge ones.
Blue and dark, stretching farther than what eyes could see.
He hovered above it and looked down.
There were creatures in the water—large, slow-moving shapes that swam like living shadows beneath the surface.
He dipped down and landed on a shore.
The sand was black. The sky was darker here. He walked along the shore and watched the sea.
Then he tried again.
He sent out a pulse of light energy into the water, hoping for a reaction from anything intelligent.
And this time, something happened.
A huge creature rose, breaking the surface in a wave.
Vexarion’s eyes shined, but the creature... it seemed... strange.
It had no eyes, only a mouth lined with blunt teeth. It stared at nothing and released a deep sound that shook the water, then... it sank back down.
"W-Wait!!"
Vexarion called out but...
He soon realized the... beast or whatever it was, couldn’t listen to him. Even if it could, it wouldn’t react to him because it... could not.
It was not intelligent enough to.
He...
He wouldn’t get anything out of it.
So he...
He left again and continued searching.

Vexarion stared at the empty air and exhaled slowly.
"Nothing, huh..."
He paused, finally accepting the truth.
"Fine,"
He whispered.
"Not here."
With those words, he left and...
He flew again.
Then, he found another world.
This one had oceans.
Huge ones.
Blue and dark, stretching farther than what eyes could see.
He hovered above it and looked down.
There were creatures in the water—large, slow-moving shapes that swam like living shadows beneath the surface.
He dipped down and landed on a shore.
The sand was black.
The sky was darker here.
He walked along the shore and watched the sea.
Then he tried again.
He sent out a pulse of light energy into the water, hoping for a reaction from anything intelligent.
And this time, something happened.
A huge creature rose, breaking the surface in a wave.
Vexarion’s eyes shined, but the creature... it seemed... strange.
It had no eyes, only a mouth lined with blunt teeth.
It stared at nothing and released a deep sound that shook the water, then... it sank back down.
"W-Wait!!"
Vexarion called out but...
He soon realized the... beast or whatever it was, couldn’t listen to him.
Even if it could, it wouldn’t react to him because it... could not.
It was not intelligent enough to.
He...
He wouldn’t get anything out of it.
So he...
He left again and continued searching.

chapters.title: Chapter 2238: She is here.
paragraphs: "W-Wait!!"
Vexarion called out but...
He soon realized the... beast, or whatever it was, couldn’t listen to him. Even if it could, it wouldn’t react to him because it... could not.
It was not intelligent enough to.
He...
He wouldn’t get anything out of it.
So he...
He left again and continued searching for another world, another clue, anything that could bring him back.
At first, he had high hopes.
Even if the worlds he went to were dead, even if the entities he encountered did not have the ability to think,
the failure only made him more determined.
He told himself these worlds were too young.
He told himself he simply needed to travel farther.
He told himself that his allies... or at least someone, something he knows, must be somewhere beyond this strange region.
He imagined it clearly.
He imagined reaching a familiar star cluster, or... or seeing a familiar world, even a ruined world, even lingering aura traces.
He imagined a city.
He imagined a cultivator sensing him and reacting.
He imagined an ally responding through the call artifact.
He imagined kneeling before Lady Seraphielle’s throne the moment he returned, telling her everything.
Not just about the Anomaly.
But about the truth.
That the real danger—
The crazy Chaos Heir, and the monster who held her hand.
He imagined saving himself.
He imagined redeeming his humiliation.
He imagined being... important again.
And that fantasy kept him moving.
Just like that, ’days’ passed.
Actually, Vexarion had stopped counting properly at some point because of how... strange the flow of time in this place was.
It didn’t stop, neither did it move back. It moved like time should but...
It simply... didn’t feel like the time flow he was familiar with.
He began noticing it in small ways.
His fatigue came too slowly sometimes, as if his body refused to acknowledge exhaustion. Then, other times, it came too quickly, like his strength vanished between one heartbeat and the next.
He thought maybe it was because of lack of rest. Yes, he was an Eternal who normally did not need sleep but... what his body and mind went through was anything but normal.
He could sense how lack of sleep would chip away at his senses and affect how he perceived things around him.
And since he had been tirelessly flying for ’days’ with no signs of the enemy catching up to him, he knew he had gotten quite far and had lost them.
A short nap was possible.
Or at least that was how he tried to convince his mind, but the moment he closed his eyes and tried to sleep—
He saw that same grin, his ears rang as that echoing, frightening laughter rang in his head, that agonizing pain that healed a long time ago but still lingered.
Sure, his mind might be trying to forget it all, but his body?
It was broken far beyond what he realized.
Sleep was not an option.
Not for now, not for... the next few millennia.
The only thing he could do was to rest in the air, still hovering, eyes half-open, senses stretched wide.
He landed on dead stars and sat in silence, forcing his mind to calm. He tried to meditate, but it didn’t work, because the moment his thoughts slowed, the memories rose.
All he could do was... move.
And as he moved, hope changed shape.
It became less like a bright flame like it was at the beginning and more like a... thin thread. A thread that he was holding with all his might, but in his mind, he knew it could snap any moment.
He continued his journey, and in his journey, he found more worlds.
Some had forests, some had deserts, some were made of stone with no water, some had storms that never ended.
Some even had life but...
It was simple, wordless, and mindless.
A life that was of no use to him.
Vexarion tried everything.
He carved symbols of Light into mountains, hoping someone would recognize them and come. He raised pillars of golden energy into the sky as beacons, leaving them behind as markers.
But when he returned hours later, those pillars had already faded, like the laws of this region refused to let such things remain.
He tried to track his path by stars, but the stars shifted too subtly, like they weren’t fixed properly yet.

He tried to force the call artifacts again and again; sometimes they flickered, sometimes they warmed, once, he even heard a faint static sound, so quiet he thought it might be his imagination, and every time it happened, it flared his hope.
He poured his energy into the artifact until the veins on his neck glowed but...
It died again.
Vexarion stared at it for a long time.
His fingers tightened.
Then, suddenly—
Bam
Crack
He threw it. The artifact flew and shattered against a rock, its pieces scattering into the dust, and Vexarion...
He watched as those pieces drifted in the space; his breathing became uneven as he realized he had momentarily lost control over himself.
He tried to think about it. Was it anger? Frustration? Hopelessness maybe? And as his thought began to wander, his mind flashed back to Sharnoth clapping, cheering for him like he was a child.
’Good job! You are doing so well!’
His stomach twisted. He pressed a hand to his chest and forced himself to breathe slowly.
Then—
"AAAAAGGGGGHHHHHHH!!!"
He screamed out loud, emptying his mind once again, letting go of all his thoughts.
"Control,"
He whispered to himself.
"Control yourself, you need to escape. You are the first that has the chance to. This wasn’t meant to be easy; you wouldn’t be the first if it was."
He began convincing himself, trying to make himself believe that what he was doing had meaning, that it would all end eventually and that he...
He would return to his world.
He looked up at the sky.
It was quiet.
Too quiet.
There were no messengers, no divine projections, no signs of the Supreme World of Light watching over creation.
It felt like he had been cut out of the Universe and thrown into a young corner no one cared about.
And that thought—
That thought was dangerous.
Because it led to another thought.
What if no one can find me?
He shook his head hard, as if he wanted to throw that thought out of his mind physically.
"No."
He muttered.
"They will.
They...must."
But even as he said it, his hope thinned again.

He started speaking less. He started flying without looking around much. He started ignoring beauty. There were places that were breathtaking—rings of floating stones around a dying star, auroras that moved like living curtains, oceans that glowed softly at night.
He did not care.
He only cared about one thing.
A sign.
A single sign that he was close. A familiar aura. A familiar constellation. A voice.
Someone.
Anyone.
At some point, he began hearing things that weren’t there.

A whisper in the wind. A sound behind him. A laugh far away. Each time, his body flinched like it had been struck. Each time, he spun around, halo flaring, light bursting out in hopes of finding something but...
Nothing.
There was only... the familiar empty space.
Space that he had now begun to hate because it made him remember...herworld.
That... grey land.
Thenowhere.
Again, to shove that thought out of his head, he pushed harder, forcefully increasing his speed until it felt like his wings were giving out. He understood it: if he slowed down, his mind would sink.
So he ran forward like a man running from a shadow that lived inside his skull.
And then—
One day, after continuing this hopeless... torturous journey for he did not know how long, something changed.

For the first time in a long, long while, Vexarion heard something that wasn’t just the sound of stars colliding, mindless beasts roaring, water falling on the ground, or the winds moving. He heard...
A voice.
A coherent voice.
A voice that did not travel through air.
A voice that did not need permission.
A voice that didn’t care about distance or strange laws.
"Children of the Universe..."
And the moment Vexarion heard it, he froze. His entire body went still, like the cosmos itself had grabbed him by the spine.
He knew that voice.
Even if he had been deaf, even if he had lost his mind, he would have known it.
Seraphielle Light.
The Infinity of Light.
His Goddess.
His Absolute.
His... salvation.
Vexarion’s eyes shined so brightly that the dark around him seemed to retreat. His chest rose sharply, like he had been drowning and finally found air.
He looked up at the sky, searching for the source.
And for the first time in what felt like forever—
He smiled.
A real smile.
Not a broken one.
Not a desperate one.
A smile filled with... belief.
"She... she is speaking.
She is here."
He whispered, voice trembling.
Finally... it worked.
Finally... Light reached him.
The sky opened.
A Veil stretched across the void.
Seraphielle’s vast, holy, and absolute face filled it.
Vexarion smiled, his eyes shining so brightly, resembling a child who saw his parent after weeks of darkness.
But then—
Then his blood turned cold.
Because behind the Veil... behind the Light...
Stood the demon that had haunted every second of his "escape."
"My toy is finally here~"

chapters.title: Chapter 2239: The two of you have a history together, correct?
paragraphs: "My toy is finally here~"
The instant Vexarion heard those words, he... froze.

For a heartbeat, he couldn’t understand what he was hearing. Every core of his being tried to deny it, twist it into something else, or pretend it was only an echo of trauma, a memory that had followed him too far.
But...
It didn’t matter.
He could try to deny it however much he liked, but it wouldn’t change the reality.
And as if she wanted it to sink in...
"See? I told you he would come on his own if we use this."
Another woman with long white hair and purple eyes, standing beside that monstrous woman, commented with a playful smile on her face.
"You wasted so much time finding him. You should have listened to what I was saying beforehand."
The woman rolled her eyes with a cute pout, but her playful words... crushed Vexarion’s entire world.
Come on his own...?
What did that mean...?
Vexarion’s mind began running wild as more and more thoughts popped up.
He had run away. He did not know how long he had been on the run, but for the last few weeks—or at least days—all he did was run, and he ran with all his might.

Sure, this monster was strong in ways he couldn’t even imagine, but even then, the Anomaly had given him quite the lead and... in his mind, Vexarion was quite positive that he had left the crazy woman behind.
And considering how... strange this region of the Universe was, finding him shouldn’t be easy, even for a monster like her.
And it was all true. For weeks, Sharnoth couldn’t find him.
Then...
Did it mean... like that woman said... instead of finding him, they... used that recording to summon him instead...?
Didn’t that mean... he ran to his nightmare... on his own?
And as if to confirm that—
That crazy woman who was currently staring at Vexarion with her intense, crimson eyes... she grinned.
That same grin...
The grin that had watched him die.
The grin that clapped when his bones were crushed.
The grin that called his screams music.
Then, the crazy woman spoke.
"You were right."
"I told you~"
The other woman shrugged.
"I shouldn’t be praising myself like this, but I am a little bit of a genius myself."
"Thank you. It is thanks to you that I finally found my toy~"
Sharnoth replied.
She was clearly addressing the woman standing next to her, but her eyes were still on him, and it wasn’t just her. The rest of the women present... they were all staring at him and...
And he recognized them.
The group had become too popular for him to not know about them.
The Leander Family.

The mercenary group that helped Sharnoth before, the mercenaries that every mercenary in the Universe had heard about because of the absurd rate at which they cleared their missions and rose in the rankings.
Of course, that was all in the past. Now it wasn’t just the mercenaries who knew about them; every being in the Universe knew.

The connection between the Anomaly, the Chain Breakers, and the Leander Family had already been made. The entire world knew the Leander Family was with the Anomaly. Everyone knew they were... a Universal threat.
And now...
They were all standing before him.
But to Vexarion—
Their presence did not matter.
His eyes...
His eyes were only focused onher.

Standing behind the Veil that covered the entire space, behind Seraphielle’s golden radiance, the woman who hovered in the space barefoot, her long grey hair drifting even though there was no wind flowing here and...
Vexarion’s breath caught in his throat.
His lungs stopped moving.
His wings, still spread behind him, went stiff like stone.
The word slipped out of him without permission.
It was the sound of a man who had pushed his body past its limits multiple times to travel through a maze, only to find himself circling back to the beginning.
And Sharnoth...
She just tilted her head and—
Her grin widened.
"You actually dared to run away."
She spoke, and those words sent tremors down Vexarion’s spine.
"You are a bad toy~"
Sharnoth spoke, her crimson eyes shining even more intensely.
"And bad toys need to be punished, don’t you think?"
She asked.
Her voice was soft and playful, almost... gentle.
And that only made it worse.
Vexarion’s knees buckled.
His instincts screamed at him to move, to attack, to fly, to do something.
But his mind—
His mind remembered too much.
The claws.
The slow tearing.
The way his heart was crushed in her palm, multiple times.
The way he had died, and then woke up again, whole, and then died again.
And again.
And again.
His stomach twisted violently.
Golden bile rose in his throat and—
"Kkhawwrrkkk!!"
He gagged, coughing hard as he spat outside, and his body seemed like it collapsed, having no energy to do anything.
But...
But even that felt meaningless.
Because the moment he lifted his head again, she was still there.
It was not a hallucination, nor an illusion.
It was real.
Real enough to... break him.
He whispered again, his eyes, his hands, his entire body shook. He backed away without even realizing it and kept stepping back.
One step.
Then another.
And another.
Like distance could save him.
Like... space meant anything.
Like he wasn’t... already trapped.
His mind began to scream.
Run.
Run.
RUN.
But... where?
Where was he supposed to go?

He had been running for weeks, maybe even months, but he still couldn’t find anything familiar. He visited worlds, saw creatures he had never once seen before. Even if it was a newly formed region, it still didn’t make sense for it to be... this absurdly large unless...
Unless he had been thinking wrong about it the whole time.
Maybe...
This wasn’t a newly formed region.
Maybe it was something else entirely, a place he... he could never leave no matter how much he tried.
And that only made sense.

Even the Light Borns, the beings known for the absolute nature of their strength, were unable to find their way out once the Anomaly took them away. How was he supposed to do what couldn’t be done in the first place?
It was impossible.
He was hoping for the impossible.
It was nothing more than wishful thinking.
Yes.
Vexarion, who, for who knows how long, had been running without thinking of giving up, ready to go against all possible odds if it meant he could escape...
was now breaking.
But then—
In his desperation, his expression hardened, and he took out all his call artifacts. Maybe... maybe... they were working now.
Maybe she could hear him!
Without waiting, he lifted the call artifact with trembling fingers, like a drowning man lifting a broken rope, and poured all his energy into them.
His veins flared gold, his halo burned above him, even the artifacts began to shine, not because they were being activated, but because the amount of energy being poured into them was too much.
But...
Nothing happened. Putting extra energy wouldn’t change anything.
The artifacts did not work.
"Work..."
Vexarion begged, his voice cracking.
"Work, damn you..."
He cursed.
But then...
"You aren’t thinking of running away from the punishment, are you?"

He heard Sharnoth’s voice again and flinched. He lifted his head to look at her, but the moment he did, he realized the woman was already standing right next to him and was now extending her palm towards him.
He tried to dodge, but the woman knew his movements and his patterns a little too well for him to do anything, so she grabbed him in an instant and—
"AAAGGGGGHHHH!!!"
He screamed as Chaos Energy poured into his body, corrupting his own energy and burning his entire body with agonizing pain in the process until...
He could no longer hold on anymore and...
He perished.
And the next instant—
Shadows covered his body, only to rebuild it again, bringing the dead Vexarion back to life.
"Haaaahh... Haaahhh... Haahhhh..."
The Aurendor Progenitor stared at the dark, hollow sky above him, his body trembling in fear of what was about to come and just like that—
The torture began again.

Once again, the Herald of Justice was killed again and again, every time in a different way, each seemingly more agonizing than the other. The man tried to fight back, run, beg, or call for his allies multiple times while screaming in agony, but it didn’t change anything.
The cycle continued endlessly until...
Vexarion broke down again.
Both his mind and body reached a condition where they no longer reacted to anything that happened outside until suddenly—
"Haaahh... I am bored now~
The toy’s no longer fun."
The crazy woman yawned.
Then, she clapped her hands and summoned someone. The one who was summoned walked out with his head hung low, but the instant Vexarion saw him, his expression changed—
It was Ythric.
His closest aide back in Aurendor.
The moment Sharnoth saw Vexarion’s reaction, she grinned.
"Recognize him?"
She asked directly. Vexarion’s eyes turned towards her and then back to his subordinate. His subordinate, however, seemed a little different. His usually bright eyes now seemed... dead.
It was almost as if he had lost himself and no longer belonged to this world.
And...
He was right.
"This is my new puppet. Seemed quite useful, so I took him, made him into what I wanted, and now he does everything I tell him to."
Sharnoth laughed as she said those words.
"The two of you have a history together, correct?
Why don’t you catch up?"
She chuckled and then—
"Toy two, take toy one away and put him in a cell. I can’t have him run away again."
She ordered, and Ythric moved, not even caring about the fact that the man he was about to capture was his previous master.

Did it mean... like that woman said... instead of finding him, they... used that recording to summon him instead...?
Didn’t that mean... he ran to his nightmare... on his own?
And as if to confirm that—
That crazy woman who was currently staring at Vexarion with her intense, crimson eyes... she grinned.
That same grin...
The grin that had watched him die.
The grin that clapped when his bones were crushed.
The grin that called his screams music.
Then, the crazy woman spoke.
"You were right."
"I told you~"
The other woman shrugged.
"I shouldn’t be praising myself like this, but I am a little bit of a genius myself."
"Thank you.
It is thanks to you that I finally found my toy~"
Sharnoth replied.
She was clearly addressing the woman standing next to her, but her eyes were still on him, and it wasn’t just her.
The rest of the women present... they were all staring at him and...
And he recognized them.
The group had become too popular for him to not know about them.
The Leander Family.

The mercenary group that helped Sharnoth before, the mercenaries that every mercenary in the Universe had heard about because of the absurd rate at which they cleared their missions and rose in the rankings.
Of course, that was all in the past.
Now it wasn’t just the mercenaries who knew about them; every being in the Universe knew.
The connection between the Anomaly, the Chain Breakers, and the Leander Family had already been made.
The entire world knew the Leander Family was with the Anomaly.
Everyone knew they were... a Universal threat.
And now...
They were all standing before him.
But to Vexarion—
Their presence did not matter.
His eyes...
His eyes were only focused onher.

Standing behind the Veil that covered the entire space, behind Seraphielle’s golden radiance, the woman who hovered in the space barefoot, her long grey hair drifting even though there was no wind flowing here and...
Vexarion’s breath caught in his throat.
His lungs stopped moving.
His wings, still spread behind him, went stiff like stone.
The word slipped out of him without permission.
It was the sound of a man who had pushed his body past its limits multiple times to travel through a maze, only to find himself circling back to the beginning.
And Sharnoth...
She just tilted her head and—
Her grin widened.
"You actually dared to run away."
She spoke, and those words sent tremors down Vexarion’s spine.
"You are a bad toy~"
Sharnoth spoke, her crimson eyes shining even more intensely.
"And bad toys need to be punished, don’t you think?"
She asked.
Her voice was soft and playful, almost... gentle.
And that only made it worse.
Vexarion’s knees buckled.
His instincts screamed at him to move, to attack, to fly, to do something.
But his mind—
His mind remembered too much.
The claws.
The slow tearing.
The way his heart was crushed in her palm, multiple times.
The way he had died, and then woke up again, whole, and then died again.
And again.
And again.
His stomach twisted violently.
Golden bile rose in his throat and—
"Kkhawwrrkkk!!"
He gagged, coughing hard as he spat outside, and his body seemed like it collapsed, having no energy to do anything.
But...
But even that felt meaningless.
Because the moment he lifted his head again, she was still there.
It was not a hallucination, nor an illusion.
It was real.
Real enough to... break him.
He whispered again, his eyes, his hands, his entire body shook.
He backed away without even realizing it and kept stepping back.
One step.
Then another.
And another.
Like distance could save him.
Like... space meant anything.
Like he wasn’t... already trapped.
His mind began to scream.
Run.
Run.
RUN.
But... where?
Where was he supposed to go?
He had been running for weeks, maybe even months, but he still couldn’t find anything familiar.
He visited worlds, saw creatures he had never once seen before.
Even if it was a newly formed region, it still didn’t make sense for it to be... this absurdly large unless...
Unless he had been thinking wrong about it the whole time.
Maybe...
This wasn’t a newly formed region.
Maybe it was something else entirely, a place he... he could never leave no matter how much he tried.
And that only made sense.
Even the Light Borns, the beings known for the absolute nature of their strength, were unable to find their way out once the Anomaly took them away.
How was he supposed to do what couldn’t be done in the first place?
It was impossible.
He was hoping for the impossible.
It was nothing more than wishful thinking.
Yes.
Vexarion, who, for who knows how long, had been running without thinking of giving up, ready to go against all possible odds if it meant he could escape...
was now breaking.
But then—
In his desperation, his expression hardened, and he took out all his call artifacts.
Maybe... maybe... they were working now.
Maybe she could hear him!
Without waiting, he lifted the call artifact with trembling fingers, like a drowning man lifting a broken rope, and poured all his energy into them.
His veins flared gold, his halo burned above him, even the artifacts began to shine, not because they were being activated, but because the amount of energy being poured into them was too much.
But...
Nothing happened.
Putting extra energy wouldn’t change anything.
The artifacts did not work.
"Work..."
Vexarion begged, his voice cracking.
"Work, damn you..."
He cursed.
But then...
"You aren’t thinking of running away from the punishment, are you?"
He heard Sharnoth’s voice again and flinched.
He lifted his head to look at her, but the moment he did, he realized the woman was already standing right next to him and was now extending her palm towards him.
He tried to dodge, but the woman knew his movements and his patterns a little too well for him to do anything, so she grabbed him in an instant and—
"AAAGGGGGHHHH!!!"
He screamed as Chaos Energy poured into his body, corrupting his own energy and burning his entire body with agonizing pain in the process until...
He could no longer hold on anymore and...
He perished.
And the next instant—
Shadows covered his body, only to rebuild it again, bringing the dead Vexarion back to life.
"Haaaahh...
Haaahhh...
Haahhhh..."
The Aurendor Progenitor stared at the dark, hollow sky above him, his body trembling in fear of what was about to come and just like that—
The torture began again.
Once again, the Herald of Justice was killed again and again, every time in a different way, each seemingly more agonizing than the other.
The man tried to fight back, run, beg, or call for his allies multiple times while screaming in agony, but it didn’t change anything.
The cycle continued endlessly until...
Vexarion broke down again.
Both his mind and body reached a condition where they no longer reacted to anything that happened outside until suddenly—
"Haaahh...
I am bored now~
The toy’s no longer fun."
The crazy woman yawned.
Then, she clapped her hands and summoned someone.
The one who was summoned walked out with his head hung low, but the instant Vexarion saw him, his expression changed—
It was Ythric.
His closest aide back in Aurendor.
The moment Sharnoth saw Vexarion’s reaction, she grinned.
"Recognize him?"
She asked directly.
Vexarion’s eyes turned towards her and then back to his subordinate.
His subordinate, however, seemed a little different.
His usually bright eyes now seemed... dead.
It was almost as if he had lost himself and no longer belonged to this world.
And...
He was right.
"This is my new puppet.
Seemed quite useful, so I took him, made him into what I wanted, and now he does everything I tell him to."
Sharnoth laughed as she said those words.
"The two of you have a history together, correct?
Why don’t you catch up?"
She chuckled and then—
"Toy two, take toy one away and put him in a cell.
I can’t have him run away again."
She ordered, and Ythric moved, not even caring about the fact that the man he was about to capture was his previous master.

chapters.title: Chapter 2240: Run...?
paragraphs: "The two of you have a history together, correct?
Why don’t you catch up?"
Sharnoth chuckled as she glanced at Vexarion.
Then, she turned towards Ythric and—
"Toy two, take toy one away and put him in a cell.
I can’t have him run away again."
She ordered, and Ythric moved, not even caring about the fact that the man he was about to capture was his previous master.

Vexarion’s eyes widened, his body trembled as he used all his might to try and move but... his body had given out. All his limbs were attacked and bruised in such a manner that they could no longer be used, at least not until he was reborn.

And even if those limbs of his could move, it wouldn’t change anything since Vexarion’s mind itself had collapsed. Even though he wanted to run, wanting and actually being able to do it were two entirely different things.
Not to mention that with Sharnoth here, it was pretty much impossible for him to leave.

So even as Ythric walked towards him, prepared to throw him inside a prison where he would be tortured whenever this crazy woman wanted for eternity, the only thing Vexarion could do was tremble, while his eyes showed different emotions.
Anger.
Fear, intense fear, and—
Plea.
A desperate plea, literal begging to be let go, in any way possible, even if it meant true death.
Yes, Vexarion stared at the man who was once his subordinate, then at Sharnoth, then at the women standing behind her and begged from them all—
But...

None of them cared. Sharnoth just grinned at him as she turned around, walking towards the rest of the women. As for the said women, they didn’t seem to care about him one bit. To him, he was just... a source of entertainment.
As for Ythric...
The man walked toward him with dead eyes that showed no reaction even when he called him hundreds of times.
Ythric did not even acknowledge his existence, almost as if his memories had been wiped out and he was turned into a clean slate that only followed orders.
In the end, the puppet picked his previous master. The weak Vexarion, who had lost the ability to move his limbs, couldn’t resist.
"Keep good care of him, I don’t want any mistakes."
Sharnoth gave her order as she raised her hand without turning back toward the two, almost as if saying goodbye.
And Ythric, who from the beginning hadn’t said a word even when his previous master called him multiple times—
"As you command, Lady Sharnoth."

He nodded calmly, his voice so subservient that even Vexarion was somewhat taken aback. He looked at the man with a betrayed look on his face, but Ythric didn’t care. To him, Vexarion was just an order.
He picked the man and started moving in a specific manner despite Vexarion’s weak struggles.

This continued for a good fifteen minutes. By now, Vexarion himself had given up on escaping. His body was too weak to resist Ythric, his mind had collapsed to the point he couldn’t even use his Aura to suppress him.
Heck, he didn’t even have enough strength to kill himself.
He was nothing more than a living dead body, a body that could only tremble... helplessly.
Until...
"Kill yourself."
Until suddenly, Vexarion heard a voice.
He asked as he looked around, trying to see where the voice came from and...
It was Ythric.
And as if Ythric knew Vexarion did not quite register his words, he repeated himself, but this time, his tone was far clearer than before.
"Lord Vexarion, you need to kill yourself, hurry!"
His words, however, only confused Vexarion even further.
Lord Vexarion...?
This was what Ythric called him back in Aurendor, when he was loyal to him, but...
Why was he doing it now...?
Especially after ignoring him while he desperately begged for help...?
And as if Ythric knew what he was thinking, he began to explain.
"You need to run! You are the only one who can!"
He raised his voice, but only a little, as if he was afraid someone else would hear them. The way he continuously looked around while talking made it clear that Ythric did not want that to happen.
Vexarion stuttered. Those words made his entire body shudder.
Run...?
Could he run away...?
Was that possible...?
"Yes!"
Ythric nodded.
"You need to kill yourself so you can rebuild your body, regaining all your energy so you can run."
"B-But you..."
Weren’t you together with that monster? Why are you helping me?

Vexarion wanted to ask, but he didn’t dare to. His mind had already collapsed to the point that even asking questions from a man who was once his subordinate made him... hesitant and fearful. His worry that something might go wrong and the torture might continue again broke him.
But Ythric knew what he was thinking, and he did not disappoint his Lord.
"She was too focused on you, so much that when she was brainwashing us, she made some mistakes, letting me find a loophole.

All this time, I was only pretending to be her puppet, like the others she had brainwashed had become. I was waiting for an opportunity to run but I didn’t get anything. There are many here stronger than me. If I disappear, they will find me and might reperform the brainwashing, this time without letting me find a loophole.
I would truly lose myself then, and I cannot allow it to happen.
So I need help and..."
Ythric looked at Vexarion with desperate eyes and—
"You are the only one who can help me."
He declared.
"You are stronger and faster than me. If given the chance, you definitely have what it takes to get away from this darned place and inform the Supreme World of Light about it and save us, save me."
Ythric poured all his intense emotions out and Vexarion...
He stayed silent.
He was different from Ythric. He had managed to escape once and he was caught. This place was absurdly large. He had been flying for months maybe and he still couldn’t find a way out.
In the end, in his desperate state, he fell for a trick so obvious and... went to that crazy woman on his own.
It was a stupid moment that had imprinted itself in his mind permanently, constantly reminding him how... foolish he was.
And after the constant reminders for... who knows how long—
Vexarion was done.
He had no intentions of running away. This wasn’t a place he could escape from. Many must have tried, but they all failed. He wouldn’t be any different.
That was how Vexarion convinced himself but—
"Please, Lord Vexarion,
Please do it for us.
For the sake of your people."
Ythric begged. Then, as if he wanted to make his offer even more tempting, he took out a piece of paper from his inventory and—
"This! Maybe you can use this!"
He spoke as he placed the paper on the ground in front of Vexarion.
It was a map.
A map that Vexarion did not recognize but... for some reason, he found the pattern inside it very familiar.
His mind began to work as the memories replayed themselves. He traced back the path he had taken when he ran away and finally—
He noticed something.
The path he had taken... it was one of the paths shown in the map.
"Sharnoth gave it to me because she wanted me to run an errand for her. Never took it back since she had already ordered me not to show it to anyone.

I have seen her puppets killing themselves just because she ordered them to, so I am assuming she never thought I, another one of her ’puppets’, would be the same and follow her orders to the very end.
She never knew I was pretending."
Ythric spoke, and Vexarion... he was staring at him in disbelief.
And once again—
The Aurendor Progenitor saw it.
Hope.
Light at the end of a long, dark tunnel.
"A-Are you saying you have been pretending to follow her orders just so you could find me and get my help...?"
He asked, still in disbelief.
"Yes."
Ythric nodded, but Vexarion—
"T-That monster wouldn’t make such a mistake."
He had his doubts.
But Ythric had a perfect answer.
"All her attention was on you ever since the beginning. Even when you left, she and her people were busy looking for you, instead of focusing on other hostages.
Maybe that’s why she made a mistake.
But I do not think I can pretend for long. A few of those women around her are quite thorough. Some already look at me with suspicious eyes; they just haven’t said anything yet."
"So you are saying I do not have much time."
Vexarion muttered as he narrowed his eyes.
And Ythric turned towards his Lord with a solemn look on his face—
"There isnotime.
Thisis theonlyopportunity you have. Once you are locked inside their prison, escaping is impossible."
He answered, telling him just how serious this matter actually was.
Vexarion still had many questions, but in the end, since he understood he was pressed for time—
"What is your plan?"
He asked directly.
Ythric pointed at a certain point in the map without waiting and—
"I believe this is the exit from this place."
He muttered, and hearing the word ’exit’ instantly made Vexarion react and turn towards Ythric.
Ythric too turned back at Vexarion and—
"I want you to get to the exit and escape.
Then return with reinforcements to get rid of both the Anomaly and the Chaos Heir."

chapters.title: Chapter 2241: You didn’t think I was actually helping you, did you?
paragraphs: "I believe this is the exit from this place."
Ythric spoke, the wordexitinstantly gripping Vexarion’s attention as Ythric continued.
"I want you to get to the exit and escape.
Then return with reinforcements to get rid of both the Anomaly and the Chaos Heir."
And Vexarion...
He did not say anything.
But his eyes—
They remained focused on the ’exit’ Ythric had pointed at for a good few seconds. Ythric didn’t say anything either. He let his lord think whatever it was he was thinking and then—
"How do you know that’s the exit?"
Vexarion asked carefully.
He had already tried to escape once and was caught, so he did not wish to make any more mistakes. He wanted to be as thorough as possible now that it was his second and even his last attempt.
But...
"I do not know for sure."
The answer he received, however, was not what he was looking forward to.
"While most of the focus was on you, Lord, I still had a few eyes on me. I couldn’t move freely; else my pretense would fall.
In these past few weeks, I have been assigned missions that required me to move all around this region, so I know most of it fairly well—most, except this.
None of the missions assigned to me needed me to get here. I assume it is because they fear that our allies might find me and come back with reinforcements."

He gave his explanation, and while Vexarion wasn’t exactly thrilled after learning that the information he was being provided was merely an assumption, especially when this time he wanted to be as thorough as possible, he...
He had no choice but to accept.
"I understand."
He nodded as he grabbed the map Ythric gave him. Ythric nodded back, then he turned around, showing his back to Vexarion, and before Vexarion could understand what he was trying to do—
"Now please attack me, Lord Justice."
Ythric requested. Vexarion frowned in confusion and Ythric—
"Make me lose consciousness. Then kill yourself, recover, and run."
Ythric then looked at Vexarion one last time and—
"Please, return quickly."
He literally begged. After all, he too did not know how long he would be able to hold on. The last thing he wanted was to have the same torturous fate as Vexarion.

Vexarion understood that. He understood the risk Ythric was taking by revealing the truth and tricking the Chaos Heir in such a manner. He understood how much bravery was needed to take a step as daring as this and he...
He couldn’t be prouder of his subordinate.
So, just for his subordinate’s sake, a determined expression appeared on Vexarion’s hopeless, defeated face and he nodded with a new shine in his eyes.
Then, he moved just as Ythric told him to. Gathering all the remaining energy in his body, he attacked Ythric to the point he lost consciousness. Then, the Aurendor Progenitor killed himself.
It was... humiliating.
Suicide was considered to be a sign of weakness. This was especially true in the eyes of Eternals, who had already reached the peak of the Universe and were known for their sheer arrogance.
Vexarion himself had laughed at quite a few Eternals who decided to take their own lives, that too, right in front of their families.
And today...
While he held the sword in his hand, prepared to kill himself—he didn’t think about any of that.
He couldn’t care less.
The people’s opinion was the least of his worries. The only thing that mattered was survival.
So—
Pierce
The Herald of Justice plunged his own sword into his chest, piercing his heart as he took his own life.
Thud
His body fell, and in the next second, the shadows surrounded him and his body was reformed again—as good as new.

It was a feeling he had gotten so used to that it now felt disgusting. For a good few seconds, he was creeped out by his own body. The deep fear that had settled into his very core kept him on edge all the time, making him think that monster might return anytime now.
And because of that—
Vexarion moved.
Flap

His wings spread wide again as his feet began floating. Then, he took the map in his hands and with another flap of his wings, he flew away, not even looking at the subordinate who had just passed out after his attack.
And just like that, the Herald of Justice ran.
Once again, the hope in his eyes that had dimmed was shining.
Once again, the scenes of returning to Lady Seraphielle and living under her protection became stronger than ever.
Once again, Vexarion, who wanted to die just a few minutes ago, wanted to... live.
But...
This did not last long.

Vexarion flew without stopping for two whole weeks. Since this time he had a map in his hand, he moved forward with a lot more assurance and confidence, and realizing the map in his mind was correct the more he moved only gave him more confidence.
But...
In the end—
After flying for two whole weeks and reaching the so-called ’exit’ point—
What the now excited and hopeful Vexarion saw... shattered his hope again.
[Children of the Universe.]
The same words.
The same voice.
The same face.
Everything that should have put him at ease and given him warmth—it was all there, but...
There was no speck of joy on Vexarion’s face.
Because behind those words, that voice and that face... stood... that monster who...
Who was now grinning at him.
"Oh? You are back again?
That was earlier than I expected."
The monster commented with a grin as she sat on the chair, placing her bare feet on top of a table. Her crimson eyes stared at Vexarion in amusement.
She was... enjoying the expression that had appeared on Vexarion’s face right now.
That crushed hope.
That despair.
That hopelessness.
That... fear.

Seeing the man who had haunted her entire life—the man who killed her father, destroyed her family and her world, and took everything she cherished away from her—have such a satisfying expression on his face...
It was... a beautiful sight.
A sight that filled the Chaos Heir with endless... happiness.
"Looks like your toy has recovered."
Just then, another voice was heard.
A voice that instantly got a reaction out of Sharnoth—
"NUX!!"
The woman stood and launched herself in a particular direction, flipping both the chair and the table she was using just now.
Nux chuckled at that behaviour and caught her. The woman wrapped herself around him like a koala and he held her back and began gently stroking her back.
And Vexarion...
He just stared at the sight in front of him in absolute disbelief.
Just... what was happening...?
He couldn’t understand.
This man... wasn’t he the Anomaly...?

From what he understood before, it was the Anomaly who was after this crazy woman. This was the reason he helped him the first time. Then... why did it feel like the crazy woman was the one who was after the Anomaly now?
Why did it all feel so... different...?
"You didn’t think I was actually helping you, did you?"
And just when such thoughts appeared in his head, the Anomaly turned towards him and spoke directly.
"W-What...?"
Those words made Vexarion blink. He didn’t understand how he was supposed to react.
"Did you truly believe I would let the man she hates the most escape in order to make her mine?
Do you take me for a fool?"
The Anomaly asked and Vexarion’s expression changed.
Did that mean that his previous escape was...
"Yes, it was all planned."

Before the words could even come out of his mouth, Nux answered. Because of his connection, he could easily read Vexarion’s thoughts anytime he wanted. This was one of the many reasons Vexarion could never actually outsmart any of them.
He had lost his independence the moment he was devoured.
As for Vexarion...
Hearing the word ’planned’ made him feel like his entire world had... collapsed.
Then, his mind connected the dots and another possibility appeared in his head. If his first escape was all planned, then what about...
"Yes, that too."
And once again, Nux, who was reading all his thoughts, nodded again and just then, with a wave of his hand, another being appeared.
It was Ythric.
"Y-You..."
And Vexarion’s eyes widened in disbelief as he collapsed on the ground.
"WHAT ARE YOU DOING HERE!?"

He raised his voice. The echo in his voice was so strong that it shook his surroundings, a voice filled with so much intense rage that if Ythric had normally heard it, his body would have flinched and then collapsed from sheer fear. But right now...
He had no reaction at all.
And the reason for that was...
"There’s no point shouting, Vexarion Aurendor.
My puppets do not fear you."
From the moment he came to Vexarion with the map, to the point he let Vexarion run away—he never was Ythric.
Ythric was never... Ythric.
It was just...
Nux and Sharnoth playing with Vexarion.
An entertaining, almost sickening game that broke Vexarion in ways he never thought was possible.

He did not say anything.

Ythric didn’t say anything either.
He let his lord think whatever it was he was thinking and then—

Vexarion asked carefully.

I assume it is because they fear that our allies might find me and come back with reinforcements."

He gave his explanation, and while Vexarion wasn’t exactly thrilled after learning that the information he was being provided was merely an assumption, especially when this time he wanted to be as thorough as possible, he...

Ythric requested.
