chapters.title: Chapter 2242: H-HOW ARE YOU H-HERE ALREADY!?
paragraphs: "There’s no point shouting, Vexarion Aurendor.
My puppets do not fear you."

Nux spoke as he looked at Vexarion with an indifferent look on his face. Vexarion’s body flinched as he remained on the ground, his gaze shifted from Nux to Ythric, who, just like Nux, looked at him with indifference, like he didn’t even recognize him.
For a moment, Vexarion was still hopeful, he believed that, like before, Ythric was still pretending, waiting for the opportunity to help him but...
"Have you lost your mind?
That quickly?"
Suddenly, Nux asked a question.
Vexarion quickly turned towards him, unable to understand, and Nux just tilted his head in confusion.
"Did you truly believe we would let a Transcendent watch over an Eternal like you?"
That question made Vexarion’s expression change.
"No matter how injured you were, how could a mere Transcendent ever stop an Eternal?
Think about it.

One of your subordinates somehow wasn’t turned into a puppet while all others were, all this while, he pretended to be one, waiting for the opportunity to meet you, and when he finally does, he gives you a map that magically leads you to the exit.
Doesn’t all this... feel a little too absurd to be a mere coincidence?"
Nux asked, and the more questions he asked, the more Vexarion’s mind began to question things around him, and the more... despair he felt.
"T-Then..."
He began to stutter.
"Then why...?"
He asked, glancing at Nux.
And that was when Nux finally grinned.
"Did you forget already?"
He began, his grin distorting his face. For a moment, Vexarion felt Sharnoth’s chaotic face superimposing with his and just then—
Nux repeated the words that were... extremely familiar.
"Because it’s fun."
Vexarion’s body shook.
The moment his mind registered those words, he felt... intense anger and hatred so strong that he wanted nothing more than to tear these two bastards into pieces, but before he could do that—
"Playing with you is fun, Vexarion Aurendor."
Nux stepped forward with a grin on his face, his golden eyes shining brightly.
"The Herald of Justice, the man who had brought ’judgement’ to thousands of worlds—
It is now time for you to receive your own judgement by the hands of none other than the one you judged the harshest."
Nux then got close to the Aurendor Progenitor, their foreheads barely a centimetre away, while their eyes were still locked on each other.
"Trust me, Vexarion Aurendor."
Nux continued with the same grin on his face.
"For the rest of Eternity, I will make your life miserable."
Those words echoed throughout the space.
"I will make you regret every choice you ever made, I will make you regret ever being born, I will make you regret... your very existence.
I will plunge your entire self into a hole of self-hatred.
You will become nothing but a pile of fear and self-loathing.
I will make you lose your mind, forget everything you knew about yourself, and become habitual to the constant pain and torture I am going to inflict on you.
And while I do that, every time you break, every time your mind is about to collapse because of everything that is happening,
I will give you hope.

A sliver of a thread, something that you would believe would pull you out of this hell, something that will make you crawl desperately, clinging to that rope like your very life depends on it, pushing past your limits multiple times just to hold that thread, and just when you are about to reach the end—
I will cut that thread.
And I will do it again and again and again.
Constantly.
Until you no longer try, no matter how many threads are placed right in front of you."

Nux whispered those words into Vexarion’s ears, and as he heard him, Vexarion couldn’t even react. His mind pictured everything Nux said and everything that had been happening to him, and a true fear hidden very, very deep inside him came out.
And Nux—
He just continued—
"Vexarion Aurendor, for destroying the life of the woman I love,
I will end you.
Not physically, because youwilllive, I assure you of that.
I will end you inside your own mind, to the point that even if Seraphielle herself is standing right in front of you, you would not move.
And I will keep going at it no matter how many centuries it takes.
That, Vexarion Aurendor, will be myrevenge."
Nux declared, and before Vexarion could say or do anything, Nux moved away. Then he glanced at Sharnoth, who he had dropped a few meters away, and nodded at her—
"Do whatever you please with him."
Saying those words, he disappeared together with Ythric. Leaving Vexarion with the monster he feared the most in his entire life.
"I’ll do as you say~"

Sharnoth smiled, her crimson eyes shining lovingly as she stared in the direction Nux was standing before he disappeared. Then, her eyes turned towards Vexarion and an amused, dangerous, sadistic grin appeared on her face.
A grin that Vexarion remembered well, a grin that he saw every time he closed his eyes, and every time he did see it, his entire body trembled in fear.
Then, Sharnoth began walking towards him.
Step Step Step

Slowly, step by step, her bare feet touching the dirty ground, but never once did the dirt stick on her. Her messy grey hair covered some parts of her face, her crimson eyes shined, her blood-red lips looked dangerously delicious. She looked like a mad goddess who had descended on the world to destroy everything and begin it anew.
It was... a divinely beautiful sight.
A sight that would bring any man to his knees and make him lose all his strength.
But...
But Vexarion was different.
When he saw Sharnoth walk towards him, he didn’t feel awe or any other described emotion. He only felt... fear.

And instead of losing all his strength, he... he became even stronger. His body, now set in flight mode, pushed itself past its limits, increasing its speed as he pushed off the ground and dashed away, flying at a speed he never thought he would reach.
A speed not many Eternals should be able to match but...
Sharnoth wasn’t just any Eternal.
The Chaos Heir began her chase. Of course, credit where credit’s due—Vexarion was indeed fast, even faster than Sharnoth, since he truly was pushing himself beyond his limits.
But...
Sharnoth did not give up. Instead, she just continued the chase with a smile on her face.
After all, the hunt was only fun when the prey tried to run and survive.

For an entire day, Vexarion gave his all and continued running desperately. He had created quite a bit of distance between them, so much that if they were facing each other in normal circumstances, he might have actually lost Sharnoth.
But...
Inside Nux’s Universe, that simply wasn’t possible. Sharnoth knew where he was all the time.
So when finally, after running for an entire day, Vexarion’s body gave in and he finally slowed down, Sharnoth appeared right behind him in three hours, making him widen his eyes in horror.
"H-HOW ARE YOU H-HERE ALREADY!?"
Vexarion screamed. Once again, he pushed his body beyond its limits and ran.
Or at least, that was what he tried to do but...
Thud
He slipped.
And with athud, he fell while Sharnoth walked towards him with the same grin on her face, without even a single drop of sweat on her skin.
It was clear that the Chaos Heir wasn’t even trying, and while Vexarion tried to fight back—
BOOOM
An absurd amount of black-purple energy appeared around Sharnoth.
The battle between the two began.
And just like that—
Vexarion’s torture began.
Again.
And once again, the same cycle began.
Fight.
Exhaustion.
Pain.
Revival.
And fight again.
And the cycle continued for... a few more weeks until once again—
Vexarion stopped resisting, even his screams stopped.
Yes, once again, his mind was broken.
And once again, both Sharnoth and Nux did not give up.
They knew the toy was broken, but it could still be repaired, so that was what they did.
Another scenario.
Another thread of... hope.
This time, it came in the form of Auren.
Like Vexarion, Auren was devoured too, and the Strongest Child of Light was turned into just another puppet for Nux’s immortal army.

So Nux used Auren, making him the saviour who had finally come to save Vexarion. For the first few minutes, Vexarion did not buy it, but once again, his hopes were lit again, especially when Auren abused him like he used to when they met, treating him like a dog.
That abuse, which once made him feel humiliated, now filled him with endless happiness, making him think that the torture was finally over.
But after flying with Auren for a few weeks, forced to keep up with the Light Born’s insane speed, Auren brought him to... Sharnoth again.
Once again, Vexarion broke.
The torture began again.
His body and mental state, which had just recovered, were ruined again.
And once the toy was broken—
Nux and Sharnoth came with another plan to repair him again.

They knew the toy was broken, but it could still be repaired, so that was what they did.
Another scenario.
Another thread of... hope.
This time, it came in the form of Auren.
Like Vexarion, Auren was devoured too, and the Strongest Child of Light was turned into just another puppet for Nux’s immortal army.
So Nux used Auren, making him the saviour who had finally come to save Vexarion.
For the first few minutes, Vexarion did not buy it, but once again, his hopes were lit again, especially when Auren abused him like he used to when they met, treating him like a dog.
That abuse, which once made him feel humiliated, now filled him with endless happiness, making him think that the torture was finally over.
But after flying with Auren for a few weeks, forced to keep up with the Light Born’s insane speed, Auren brought him to...
Sharnoth again.
Once again, Vexarion broke.
The torture began again.
His body and mental state, which had just recovered, were ruined again.
And once the toy was broken—
Nux and Sharnoth came with another plan to repair him again.

chapters.title: Chapter 2243: Bring it on.
paragraphs: BOOOOOM
Sharnoth’s chaos blast sent Vexarion crashing into the ground again.
His body rolled once... twice... and then... it stopped.
And this time, Vexarion did not stand up again, nor did he scream. Heck, he didn’t even let out a groan.
He just... lay there, staring upward with wide, unfocused eyes.
"Oh my~
You aren’t hurt, are you?
Was I too harsh??"
Sharnoth approached him with a grin, expecting him to tremble, to crawl away, to push his broken body one more time.
But...
Vexarion didn’t do anything.
He simply... stared above.
And that made Sharnoth tilt her head in confusion.

The Chaos Heir crouched next to him and grabbed his head, lifting his face. She expected a reaction just from this action alone, maybe a scream of pain, a flinch of terror, or even a flare of anger but...
Again, there was nothing.
There weren’t even micro reactions.
His pupils did not tighten.
His eyelids did not blink.
His throat did not swallow.
He looked alive only because his chest still moved, that too, barely.
Sharnoth called out, her head now even more tilted, showing how confused she was.
And Vexarion did not react.
Not a flinch.
Not a twitch.
Not even the faint recognition he used to show whenever he saw her.
Just then, Nux walked behind her and looked down at the Eternal, and seeing those empty eyes and sensing his empty head—
He understood it.
"He’s... gone,"
He spoke in a slow voice, and his words only made Sharnoth more confused.
"Gone where?"
She asked.
"Inside."
Nux answered as he tapped Vexarion’s forehead with his shoe, a thin ripple of dark energy passed through Vexarion’s head but again—
Nothing happened.
There was no resistance.
No mental pushback.
No spark of... self.
Only emptiness.
Empty, endless silence.
"He’s not frozen,"
Nux continued.
"He’s not pretending.
Nor is he hiding."
"...Then what is this?"
Sharnoth asked.
"Complete collapse."
Nux answered in a flat voice.
"Collapse?"
Sharnoth frowned.
"He broke."
Nux nodded, staring at the body beneath him.
"Broken all the way.
And this time—
It’s permanent."
Sharnoth leaned closer, examining Vexarion’s eyes.
After everything that had been done to him, an action like this would have guaranteed a strong reaction, but this time—
His eyes reflected no fear, hatred, despair, or even confusion.
There was just...
Absence.
"Is he... catatonic?"
Sharnoth questioned, her fingers still knocking on Vexarion’s head as if that would wake him up.
Nux, on the other hand, shook his head.
"No.
He isn’t catatonic, shocked, or unconscious."
"Then what is he?"
Sharnoth asked as she looked at Nux.
"A body that lost its mind."
Nux answered without any change in his expression; after all, he didn’t feel particularly bad. He had no soft spot for someone like Vexarion.
Sharnoth, on the other hand, blinked.
"...You mean he—"
"Yes."
Nux nodded before the Chaos Heir could even complete.
"His core self is gone."
Nux commented as if he was passing a statement. Then, he shrugged.
"It happened a lot faster than I predicted. Just a few hours ago, his mind was still constantly thinking of ways to get out of this situation.
Just what did you do to him for him to be crushed to this degree in just a few hours?"
He couldn’t help but ask.
And Sharnoth...
"I played?"
She answered innocently as she poked Vexarion’s cheek. His head rocked from the touch, eyes still fixed forward. His lips hung slightly parted.
Again, there was no reaction.
"Can’t we fix it?"
She asked casually, and Nux shook his head.
"No.
There is nothing left to fix."
Sharnoth slowly stood up, her expression changing from playful to... quietly amazed.
She stared at Vexarion like she was staring at an artifact she had accidentally broken.
"A toy without a mind is useless,"
She murmured.
"He can’t even feel scared now."
"That’s because fear requires consciousness, and he doesn’t have one anymore."
Nux answered.
Bored, Sharnoth kicked lightly at Vexarion’s leg.
His leg moved from the force... then went still again.
It was like pushing a dead branch.
"So it won’t even scream now?"
Sharnoth asked one last time. She looked like a child still clinging to the hope that there might be ’something’ left of her toy.
But...
"He won’t scream,
He won’t beg.
He won’t run.
He won’t... think."
Nux answered. Then, he paused for a moment as he stared at the broken toy and then—
"He won’t... come back, ever."
"Is he... dead?"
Sharnoth questioned with a frown. Shouldn’t they be able to solve it by killing him? He should return to normal after reviving, no?
But again—
"No."
Nux shook his head.
This time, he crouched beside the Eternal, as if inspecting him closely.
"His body is very much alive.
His energy is still flowing.
His heart is beating properly as well."
He tapped Vexarion’s forehead.
"But the person... is gone."
"No memories?"
Sharnoth asked.
"No self,"
Nux corrected.
"No sense of identity.
No thoughts.
No emotions.
No dreams."
Then, Nux stood up and stretched his body as if this was no longer exciting.
"He is an empty vessel.
Absolutely useless to us.
Well, I can temper his mind, implant fake memories, and recruit him into the Immortal Army. That is one thing he can be used for.
But that being will no longer be Vexarion."
He commented.
Sharnoth stared at her toy for another long moment.
Then, she sighed.
"That’s disappointing."
She turned away, even more bored.
Nux remained a moment longer.
He looked at the Herald of Justice, at the once proud Eternal who had judged worlds, commanded armies, and stood above all—a being who had now become... nothing more than a breathing statue.
A hollow shell.
A quiet corpse that couldn’t even die.
Then, he just shrugged.
"You did well."
He praised the living corpse after secretly glancing at the bored Sharnoth.
Nux wasn’t the sentimental type anyway; he had no interest in thinking about deep philosophical thoughts after seeing such a tragic end of such a powerful soul.
Not when he had ’other goals’ in his head.
"Rest well.
If you can, not that I care."
He shrugged, then he walked away.
Sharnoth followed him, humming softly as she looked around in boredom.
Behind them—
Vexarion remained lying in the dirt, eyes wide, staring at nothing and seeing nothing.
His breathing was still slow.
His body was still warm.
His heart was still beating rhythmically.
But the mind inside was... gone forever.
The Herald of Justice had finally escaped the torture.
By... erasing himself.
A permanent end.
A silent one.
And after this—
The Universe will never hear the name Vexarion Aurendor again.
On the other side, Sharnoth kicked a chunk of shattered obsidian across the ruined floor.
It skidded, sparked, and died.
And Sharnoth...
She had the same, constant look on her face.
Boring.
It was all boring.
She continued to walk in circles, returning to where Vexarion was and poked his lifeless leg again with the tip of her boot.
There was no twitch.
No scream.
No... fun.
"Haaaaahh..."
A long, dramatic sigh escaped her red lips.
"Useless toy."
She muttered in a flat voice full of disappointment.

She spun on her heel and started walking away from the broken Eternity. Her steps were bouncy, almost skipping, but the glee that was usually seen in her crimson eyes had dimmed to a dull, restless glow.
She hummed a tuneless, jagged melody and dragged one clawed finger along the cracked wall, leaving glowing purple scratches that hissed and smoked.
Behind her, Nux watched in silence.
He had been watching for a good few minutes now. His golden eyes tracked her every restless bounce, every sway of her long hair, every disappointed little kick at debris.
He knew that look.
The Chaos Heir was bored.
And in her case, boredom was a bomb with a very short fuse.
Just then—
A slow, predatory smile curved his lips.
This was it.
This was his moment.
He took one step.
Then another.
Slowly. Deliberately. As if he wanted her to know he was coming.
Sharnoth’s humming faltered.
Her long gray ear twitched.
Just then, as if to make sure, Nux’s step became louder, his shoes scraping over hard ground in a purposeful manner.
Just then, Sharnoth moved her head. She didn’t look straight at him, just enough to catch him in her peripheral vision, and as if understanding what game he was playing—
Her crimson eyes shined and her pupils dilated into thin, excited slits.
"Ohhh?"
A sharp, delighted grin appeared on her face.
"You’re coming after me now~?"
She asked.
Nux didn’t answer with words; he simply walked faster.
"Kek!"
Sharnoth squealed—a sound that was half-laughter, half... feral shriek—and then—
She bolted.
She didn’t run like prey; she ran like a storm that was given legs.
Absurd amounts of Chaos energy crackled wherever she went, the ground beneath her feet shattered with every step she took, while purple-black lightning arced between her horns.
She vaulted over a fallen pillar, laughing wildly as she twisted mid-air, her torn battle-dress fluttering behind her like broken wings.
Nux followed.
Even now, he wasn’t running; he was just... walking quickly, without any effort, but every time Sharnoth glanced back—
He was closer, his golden eyes locked on her like a hunter who already knew the kill was his.
"You won’t win!"
She laughed as she gathered a ridiculous amount of Chaos energy, and Nux—
"Bring it on."
He grinned back.

chapters.title: Chapter 2244: Don’t forget what you said. *
paragraphs: Blue Ball warning.
"You won’t win!"
She laughed as she gathered ridiculous amount of Chaos Energy and Nux—
"Bring it on."
He grinned back.
And Sharnoth—
BOOOM BOOOM BOOOM

She casually threw multiple blast of chaos over shoulder, chaos blast large enough to vaporise cities in an instant. Of course, The Chaos Heir knew these blasts wouldn’t do anything, she had tried to use far stronger ones before and even they failed, let alone these little ones. She just did it to lighten the surroundings and see some pretty sparks.
And as expected—
Nux sidestepped, dodging the blasts without even breaking his rhythm, the energy destroyed everything around him beside him.
Clap Clap Clap
And Sharnoth clapped her hands in glee.
"Yes! Good! Keep dodging like that!"
She laughed.
Then, she darted left, leaped onto a shattered throne, used it as a springboard to flip backward over his head—
—but Nux was already there.
His hand snapped out, fingers closing around her short tail mid-flip.
"Aah!"
Sharnoth yelped in surprise, then—she grinned and—
Puff
Her entire body turned into Chaotic Mist and reappeared a few meters apart, outside of Nux’s grasp.
"Hehe~ Not so easy~"
She grinned as she landed on her feed.

And Nux grinned as well, he extended his hand again, this time, so quickly that the Chaos Heir couldn’t even react. Then, he pulled her close, so hard that her back slammed against his chest, his one arm banded around her waist and the other hand fisted in her grey hair, tilting her head back in a way that her crimson eyes met his.
That was when he finally had a close look on her face.
The Chaos Heir was breathless, still grinning even after she was caught, Vexarion’s blood still streaked across her cheeks, while her eyes...
Her wild crimson eyes stared at Nux with a bright, strong, glow.
"Got you~"
Nux murmured in a low, dark voice as he wiped Vexarion’s blood of her face, his golden eyes shining with a possessive light.
Seeing that—
Sharnoth’s grin stretched wider—too wide, revealing almost all her teeth while her claws dug into his forearm.
"No you did not!"
She laughed in a high pitched voice then slammed her head back, cracking her horn against his jaw—
—and wrenched free in the same motion, laughing like a mad thing as she sprinted again.
Nux licked the tiny bead of blood from his lip as he watched the woman move farther and farther, and his eyes burned brighter.
The game was on.
Sharnoth ran through the shattered chamber like a bolt of lightning. Her bare feet slapped against cracked marble, leaving traces of sparks everywhere she moved.
"HAHAHAHA~~"
As she moved, her high pitched, wild, unstoppable laughed echoed throughout the chamber. Nux smiled and started following her again.

Just like before, he didn’t change his style, he walked slowly, dodging everything Sharnoth threw at him with grace, all the Chaos Energy Sharnoth put around him to slow him down simply passed through him.
His physical body was simply too strong to be affected by energies around it, not when he was in his own Universe, at his strongest.
From the beginning of the chase, he did not slow down even once.
"HAHAHAHA!!!
NUX!
You are the best!!"
Sharnoth laughed again, she had been ’fighting’ Vexarion for a long long time now, if that could even be called a fight.
It was a one sided beating, Vexarion never once managed to put up resistance amusing enough for Sharnoth to be entertained.
It was... boring.
Even though his screams pleased her...
It was all still... boring.
Deep inside, Sharnoth craved a fight.
A challenge.
Something that would fill her with... excitement.
And that was when Nux appeared. Unlike Vexarion, he wasn’t weak, infact, he was far stronger. Sharnoth had seen it on her own.
If it was Nux, she could go all out without fearing that it might break him too soon.
And that was what she did.
BOOOM BOOOM BOOOM

She let all out, without holding back, her eyes wide with a maniacal joy. And Nux? He took the attack without a second of hesitation. After all, he knew an attack of this level was never going to hurt him.
Yes, it was sheer arrogance.
Arrogance that would have offended it was someone normal, but Sharnoth was far from normal, this unfiltered arrogance only attracted her more.
"You are slowing down, Nux~"

She laughed as she continued to run. Her attacks never slowed down, not even once, a few even managed to successfully catch Nux, who couldn’t dodge them in time since his mind was too busy thinking some ’other things he was about to do.’
But then—
"Am I?"
Hearing Sharnoth and realizing that the woman was getting more... naughty, Nux grinned. Then, he teleported.
Appearing right in in her path, Sharnoth blinked, a little confused, but her body had already skidded to stop.
Then—
Clap Clap Clap
She clapped with a childish, excited look on her face, then lunged at him, prepared for another attack.
Nux dodged quickly and before the woman to react, he caught her again, this time, his hands gripping her thighs.
"Nu—"
The woman tried to resist but Nux spun, slamming her back against the nearest wall.
BAM
Crack

The stone cracked under the impact and Sharnoth’s legs naturally wrapped around his waist. An action that surprised even Sharnoth herself, after all, she did not do it on her own. At the very least, her mind wasn’t conscious of it.
It was... her body.
The two Sharnoth’s shares the same body, so clearly, when Nux spent time with ’other’ Sharnoth and took her first time, Sharnoth’s body changed... for both of them.
It developed a few... muscle memories...
And this...
This was one of those memories.

And these memories did not stop there, the moment the first memory kicked in, the rest of Sharnoth’s body began recalling...othermemories. Especially her lower body, more specifically, her... innermost region.
"Hnnnhhh~"
Sharnoth’s body trembled, her vaginal walls felt an itch so strong that for a moment, she couldn’t think of anything else but that uncomfortable feeling down there.
Without thinking, her hips began to move, stroking in the empty air on their own as if that might help with the itch but...
Nothing happened.
"Haahnnhh..."
All the excitement on her face began to disappear, turning into something more... tamer. Her vision turned hazy and from her hazy vision, she looked at Nux’s lips.
Just then, an uncontrollable urge took over her and—
Bite
She bit his lower lip, hard.
"Uggghh!!"
Nux groaned in pain as blood came out, a sight that should have horrified normal people, but Sharnoth.
Her crimson eyes shined brighter as she began sucking the blood like a vampire and enjoying every moment of that sweet irony taste.
"More,"
She demanded in a hazy, needy voice.
"More! More! More!"
She continued without shame, wrapping not just her legs, but her entire body around him.
"Ugghhh..."
Nux growled as his hands wrapped around her as well. It was painful, yes, but it was much more pleasurable than painful.
Without waiting, he kissed back.

His mouth crashed onto hers—teeth clashing, tongues fighting. He kissed her like he wanted to devour her whole and Sharnoth kissed back just as fiercely, her claws raking down his shoulders, tearing through his clothes.

Nux took advantage of the situation, one of his hands slid up her dress, palming her breast roughly. He gave a hard pinch to the slate-gray nipple between his fingers then rolled it, tugging until she arched and whined into his mouth.
"MMnnhffff~~"
A muffled whatever came out of her mouth as Sharnoth broke the kiss with a gasp, her head falling back against the wall as her long gray ears twitched.
After the kiss, going back was impossible. The kiss acted like an anchor, making her body instantly recall everything that happened to it just a few weeks ago and... it trembled.
Desperately.
Needily.

Her vaginal walls throbbed, as if screaming for Nux. The message was so strong that even Sharnoth, who wasn’t just new to this but actually feared sex after everything she had seen in the past only had one thing to say.
"Inside."
She demanded, voice shaking with intense, raw desire.
Her crimson eyes then looked right into Nux’s golden eyes and—
"Want you inside now! Want you to fill me! Want you to fuck me until I can’t walk again!
Own me!
Do whatever you want with me!
Make me so I only think of you!
I no longer want a toy!
I want tobea toy.
Your Toy."

The crazy, messed up words were spoken, words that would make any man raise his eyebrow, especially when the woman grabbed Nux’s hand and placed it on her neck, almost as if she was giving her ownership to him.

The bed itself was vast—wide enough for dozens. It was draped in layers of black silk that looked like... liquid shadow.
The air smelled faintly of the cool and sweet midnight flowers. Quite different from what it should have smelled like, especially considering everything that had happened inside this room.

Not that anyone familiar with the chambers Nux had created for his women would be surprised; these rooms were no different than living entities made to suit the women’s taste. Everything in here was personalized just for them, and the rooms had self-cleaning features.
So while Shadow slept peacefully, her room erased the remains of all the ’activities’ that were done here on its own.

BOOOM

"Sister Shadow!"

Her groggy eyes then fell on the people who had rudely barged into her chamber. Then, she narrowed her eyes, almost as if she couldn’t recognize them and was thinking hard.

And while Shadow was still trying to gather her thoughts and return to reality, another voice entered her ear, a voice she recognized quite well.

"Can you look into her mind and see if she is hiding something from us?"

Amaya, who could tell what her mother was thinking, answered in a snap, making everything clear.
Riona just smiled at her words, not saying anything, and that reaction alone made Amaya raise her eyebrows, making her explain even further.
"As for me coming here, there is no excuse.
I came here because I need her to do something for me.
The rest of you just tagged along with me."
She snorted.
Riona laughed even more.
As for others—
"I didn’t tag along with you.
I want answers too."
Aeliana answered in a snap—the last thing she wanted was for the Devourer to think she was following her.
"Me too."
Felberta nodded as well, her expression looking much more solemn than normal.
The rest of the women nodded as well.
Skyla showed her usual excitement, while Lyriana remained silent.
But the elf too was the same; she needed an answer as well and was looking at Shadow like a predator, almost as if she was prepared to use force if she had to.
And while the women talked inside Shadow’s room like they owned the place, the woman in question—
Her mind finally cleared up a little, her hazy, blank memories returning to her as her eyes finally fell on everyone around her.
"What the hell are all of you doing here?"
She asked directly, in a hoarse, sleepy voice.
"How long were you planning to sleep?"
Amaya questioned back.
"What...?"
Shadow did not understand.
"It’s been a month."
Lane informed, and the moment she realized that, Shadow froze.
After all, she too understood how strange it was.
She muttered out loud, the confusion on her face couldn’t be clearer.
"Are you alright?"
Evane asked out of concern as she gently held Shadow’s hand.
Shadow did not know how to answer that.
"I feel strange."
She muttered slowly, and those words made every woman present frown in worry.
Everyone—even Amaya—took a step forward, looking at Shadow in concern, but just then—
"I feel... much better than before...?"
Shadow opened her mouth, and Aisha’s mouth twitched in annoyance.
"Are you... rubbing it on us?"
The moment those words were said, all the concerned looks on the women disappeared into thin air, replaced by clear annoyance and even anger.
Evane too tightened her grip, almost as if she wanted to crush the woman’s hand.
And Shadow—
"No!
No!
I am not trying to rub it in—"
Shadow tried to explain herself, but just then—
"Whatever.
It is not like this is the first time she has done that."
Felberta waved her hand.
Then, she looked at Shadow with a solemn look on her face and—
"Leave that aside.
We are here because we wish to know something, and only you can help us."
"What do you mean?"
Shadow frowned; even though she wanted to explain herself, Felberta’s words attracted her attention.
And Felberta—
"Allura."
She took a name.
"Can you look into her mind and see if she is hiding something from us?"

chapters.title: Chapter 2248: Authority of Universe’s First Goddess.
paragraphs: "What do you mean?"
Shadow frowned, even though she wanted to explain herself, Felberta’s words attracted her attention.
And Felberta—
"Allura."
She said a name.
"Can you look into her mind and see if she is hiding something from us?"
Shadow blinked slowly, still half wrapped in sheets, still trying to drag her thoughts out of sleep.
And when the meaning of those words finally reached her—
"Read her mind...?"
She repeated in a low, uncertain voice.
For a moment, the entire room went quiet.

Shadow’s eyes moved from Felberta to the others. Aeliana’s stare was sharp. Lyriana’s eyes looked cold enough to cut. Skyla leaned forward like she was about to explode with curiosity. Even Lane, who usually kept her tone calm, looked somewhat tense.
Shadow sat up slightly, pulling the black silk higher. Of course, the women didn’t care about these people looking at her naked body—
in fact, if the mood was any lighter, she would have jumped on them naked just to annoy them.
But right now, she could sense the strange solemnity in the mood—solemnity so strong that even she didn’t feel like it was the right moment to pull a stunt like that.
Therefore, she held back her urges and levelled herself with the rest of the room.
"I... don’t usually do that,"
She muttered with an uncertain look on her face.
Felberta didn’t say anything; she just watched her. Almost as if she was giving Shadow time to correct herself.
But Shadow didn’t give in.
She *couldn’t* give in.
"It crosses a boundary,"
She tried to explain herself.
"I don’t like stepping into someone’s head unless I have to."
And for a moment, it seemed like what she was saying made sense—
that it *would* work and the women would listen to Shadow and drop the idea.
But then—
"Don’t think we forgot what you did to Sharnoth."
Amaya’s cold voice cut through the silence and in an instant—
Shadow froze.
Her eyes widened a little, as if trying to recall what Amaya was talking about. Then, when her still sleepy mind finally made the link, her gaze shifted away.
And slowly... she rubbed the back of her head, as if her skull itself was uncomfortable under that sentence.
The guilt was obvious.
She tried to smile.
It came out sheepish.
"That was... a mistake,"
Shadow said, like she was confessing to stealing sweets, not breaking a rule inside the family.
Then, she used the method that worked all the time—
smiling brightly and acting cute.
"I mean, you know what kind of situation she had put me into, I had no oth—"
"Enough."
Amaya waved her hand as if she was swatting away smoke.
"I don’t care."
Her dark black eyes narrowed.
"Do what you are told."
She ordered in her same cold voice and—
Shadow’s smile died.
She did not like being ordered around like that.
But at the same time, Amaya’s tone made her realize that the situation was much more serious than she previously believed.
She frowned, then, instead of Amaya—who clearly seemed on edge—she glanced at Felberta instead.
"Why?"
She asked.
"Why do you want me to do this?"
"She seems to be hiding something,"
Felberta answered in a simple manner.
Shadow stared at her for a moment and then—
"...And you want to read her mind because of that?"
She raised an eyebrow.
"Yes,"
Felberta, however, despite the look Shadow was giving her, did not step back.
And Shadow—
"Haaaahh..."
She exhaled as her body leaned back slightly, eyes half-open, thinking.
"Nux didn’t like it last time."
She muttered to herself—well, at least that was how she acted. But it was clear she was trying to come up with an excuse and she wanted the women to hear her.
Her gaze flickered to Amaya for a second, then back to Felberta.
"He doesn’t like when I use that power,"
Shadow spoke directly.
"He said it’s... invasive, and Sharnoth’s family now. I can’t use the power on family, else I’d be peeking into your minds every chance I get.
So sorry, no matter how much you want it, I won’t do something that would make Nux sad."
The moment those words left her mouth—
"Just do it."
Felberta snapped.
Of course, unlike Amaya, her voice wasn’t loud, but it was sharp enough to make everyone flinch. After all, Felberta rarely lost her calm like that.
And that outburst made Shadow blink, almost moving back a little.
Felberta, however, stepped forward. Then, she looked into Shadow’s eyes with a clear, clean look on her face.
"Do it.
I will take full responsibility,"
She declared.
"If Nux asks, I’ll tell him it was my decision. I’ll tell him I pushed you. I’ll tell him I forced this."
Shadow stared at her.
"You’re serious,"
She whispered.
The Universe’s First Goddess could tell Felberta wasn’t bluffing.
She was serious.
Something was bothering her and... she wanted to know what it was.
Felberta nodded.
"Find what she has been hiding,"
She requested.
Even Lane stepped forward and—
"She has been acting... off,"
She added in a stiff voice.
"As if you would know."
Shadow rolled her eyes.
Who would know Lane better than her?
The Shadow Demon’s mind only thinks and cares about Nux; she would almost never notice whenever *something’s off* unless it is directly related to Nux.
"No, she’s right."
Aisha spoke up as well.
And her words held quite a bit of weight; after all, she could be called the closest to Allura.
"She smiles normally, she talks normally, but it feels like she keeps stopping herself from saying something."
The Succubus spoke.
"And she avoids looking at us when we mention certain things,"
Lane nodded.
"Like she’s scared we’ll notice."
"She also has this... strangely... superior aura. As if she thinks she is better than us.
It is annoying."
Edda muttered. She looked... frustrated.
And again, like Aisha, she too was close to Allura, so her words meant a lot as well.
"She’s been... glowing,"
Not wanting to stay out of the conversation, Skyla added with a confused look on her face.
"Not literally glowing of course.
But like... she’s happy.
Too happy."
"She is definitely hiding something,"
Lyriana spoke in a flat voice and the rest of the women nodded, agreeing to everything that was said.
Shadow looked at all of them, a little surprised, even overwhelmed.
"You know... most of our thoughts are open to each other,"
She spoke as she looked at the women present in the room. Her expression finally matched her perfect, goddess-like, solemn face.
"That’s how our bond works. You can feel emotions, you can sense intent. You can even catch some surface thoughts."
The women nodded.
They knew all of this.
Shadow’s voice became quieter.
"But if someone doesn’t want to share something... they can hide it.
Completely."
The women nodded again.
They knew that as well.
"That’s what I think she’s doing,"
Felberta spoke.
"She’s hiding something important, purposefully."
Shadow’s eyes moved to the side, as if she were looking at something far away.
Her expression changed slightly—less sleepy, more... aware.
Then she spoke again.
"There’s a difference between what you can sense... and what I can see."
The room grew even quieter.
Even Amaya stopped speaking.
"My status... as the Universe’s First Goddess,"
Shadow continued.
"And as its Soul... lets me peek deeper."
The women stared.
"Anyone connected to this Universe... is connected to me.
Allura is no exception."
"So you can... see everything?"
Aeliana asked as she narrowed her eyes. She knew it to some extent, but nothing was clear.
And when Shadow was finally clarifying it...
She did not like it.
"I can,"
Shadow admitted.
"But I don’t.
As I said, Nux doesn’t like it.
I don’t either.
I don’t want to become... that kind of existence."
Silence fell over the room.
For a good few seconds, no one spoke, until Felberta stepped closer again and—
"Please,"
She requested.
"Just this once."
Shadow looked at Felberta for a long moment, then, she stared at the rest of the women who were looking at her with similar gazes—
And finally, she gave in.
"...Fine."
The Universe’s First Goddess closed her eyes.
For a moment, the room felt different. The starlight motes stopped drifting. The galaxies on the walls slowed, almost like they were holding their breath.
Shadow’s aura didn’t explode, didn’t flare, didn’t show off.
It simply... sank inward.
Like she was falling into herself. Tapping into her connection to the very Universe, and as the connection stretched—
A thread moved.
Allura’s thread.
A thread that had always been there.
And when, in her mind, Shadow reached for it—
Her expression changed within seconds and—
Her lips parted slightly.
At the reaction, the women instantly gathered closer.
Felberta stepped forward first, her voice tense.
"What? What did you see?"
Shadow didn’t answer immediately.
She looked like she had forgotten she was even in a room.
Then she slowly swallowed.
And her voice came out small, almost stunned.
"Allura... she...
She is pregnant."

chapters.title: Chapter 2249: Stop. That is enough.
paragraphs: "Allura... she...
She is pregnant."
Shadow spoke with a shocked look on her face and for a heartbeat, nobody moved.
Then—
"...what?"
Skyla blurted out, her eyes wide in surprise.
Aeliana’s eyes widened sharply, then narrowed, like she didn’t believe it.
Felberta froze completely.
Lane’s hand rose to her lips.
Even Lyriana’s cold expression cracked for a second.
As for Amaya...
She froze. Completely.
"...Pregnant?"
Felberta repeated, as if unsure of what she had just heard.
"Yes,"
Shadow nodded slowly.
"She’s pregnant."
And as the words settled into the room—
It was like time stopped.

The floating motes of starlight above the bed hung in place. The galaxies painted on the walls slowed until they were barely moving. Even the shadow-silk sheets around Shadow’s body stopped shifting, as if the room itself didn’t know how to react to news that big.
Then—
Felberta’s fingers twitched—like something inside her tried to grab the air and couldn’t.
Her wide... empty eyes stayed fixed on Shadow, as if her mind was refusing to accept the words.
Pregnant.
A child...
Nux’s child...
Felberta had been the first.
The first to find him.
The first to see him when he had nothing.
The first to make him hers, before the others appeared, before the family became what it was now.
She had to share him, yes.

And honestly, at this point, she didn’t mind. She actually thought of these women like her sisters, people who kept her company all the time. She was actually quite close to them and had accepted them all.
But...
Even then—
Her title still mattered, at least to her.
The First wife.
And in her heart, in a place she rarely showed, she had always believed something else would be first too.
His first child.
It was only right.
It was only fair.
Was it not?
Nux’s first child should have been hers by right.
And when she realized it wasn’t... she... was not happy.
To Felberta, this was important.
She had trained herself to not want it yet. To not... reach for it yet.
After all, it wasn’t safe.
For a long time, their lives had been nothing but movement.
Running.
Hiding.
Fighting.
Challenging... the impossible.
Nux had been throwing himself at monsters that once had the power to erase him with a mere thought.
Be it the King of the Skyfall Kingdom, the Pseudo Sage of the Forgotten Continent, the Dragon Lord of Yrniel, or World Leaders of different Worlds they had been to.
When they first learned about them, these were all existences far stronger than any of them and even then—
Nux did not back down, he challenged them all.
Again and again.
Like he didn’t know fear.
Like he didn’t know the meaning of "too far."
And in a life like that—
Bringing a newborn child... would have been madness.
Sure, they were strong, maybe even strong enough to protect the child if they had to but...
A newborn baby is fragile.
A newborn baby needed time.
A newborn baby needed peace.
He needed a home that didn’t shake every day because the Universe itself was angry.
Felberta understood that earlier than most.
And she had held back.
Not once.
Not twice.
For years.
For... centuries even.
At their level, pregnancy wasn’t some accident that happened because passion got out of hand.
It was a choice.
They could decide.
They had learned that truth a long, long time ago—back when the System still wrapped around their lives like invisible chains and rules.
Back then, even during intimacy, the System pushed everything in one direction.
Nux’s ’fluids’ didn’t become a seed of life.
They became fuel.
It flowed into the women like pure nourishment, strengthening their cores, expanding their foundations, pushing their cultivation forward.
That was why, even after their intimate sessions were so... long, none of the women got pregnant.
Because the System gave the ’energy’ that Nux released a purpose.
And it wasn’t to create a child.
Later, after Nux broke free from the System’s grip—after their understanding deepened, after their bodies became more than the System’s rules—
They learned the other truth.
Theycouldstill get pregnant.
They simply had to allow it.
They had to stop the flow from being consumed as power... and let it become life.
It was a simple choice.
But...
It was also a choice that had a terrifying consequence.
A child in circumstances as unstable and dangerous as theirs? With how protective Nux was of his Family, it would basically cripple all his movements.
And the women, even those who had thought about it and wanted it much more desperately than anyone else, understood it.
This was the reason Felberta and others always stopped themselves at the last moment.
Not yet.
Not while we’re still hunted.
Not while our enemies might come to us anytime.
Not while the Universe itself is shaking from anger.
These thoughts were how the women, especially Felberta, had lived, this was how she had survived.
And then—
Their Universe became complete.
A true base.
A true... home.
A place no outsider could find so easily.
A place wrapped in protection so deep that inside it they felt... untouchable. And to some extent, they were.
Here, they had... close to absolute control.
And for the first time... Felberta’s thoughts changed.
For the first time, it wasn’t... crazy anymore.
It became possible.
Felberta had started thinking:
Soon.
Maybe soon.
Maybe I’ll talk to Nux.
Maybe we can plan it together.
And no, it wasn’t because she wanted to ’win’ against the others. Well, at some level, she did. After all, Felberta too was selfish at some level.
But the much stronger reason was because she wanted to see—
She wanted to see Nux smile that way.
That soft smile.
The smile a father had when he held his child.
She wanted to see Nux carrying their child. That thought alone made her heart feel at ease—
It was a feeling so strong that her mind refused to imagine it.
She wanted toseeit, for real.
Before anyone else.
But now—
Allura had taken a step forward.
And that "first" was gone.
Felberta’s chest tightened at that thought.
So much that for a long moment, she couldn’t move. The entire room felt her emotion.
Of course, she wasn’t angry. She did not hate Allura, she couldn’t possibly hate her sister. She was just... frustrated.
A silent, bitter frustration that didn’t know where to go. It just... sat inside her like a stone, refusing to diminish and Felberta... she remained silent.
What else could she even do?
Well, at least that was what the first wife thought.
But...
Not everyone had self-control as strong as hers.
Especially a certain devourer whose attachment to her husband was... quite distorted in a strange manner.
For a moment, just like the rest, Amaya was frozen.
Her dark eyes had gone blank, her body stiff, like someone had poured cold water into her very veins, numbing them down.
But then—
Amaya’s gaze sharpened and together with her gaze, the very air around her changed.
Then—
BOOOOOOOOOM
Her Aura exploded.
Ridiculous amounts of devouring energy gathered around her, devouring the very room they were in.
The light motes inside trembled, as if screaming, begging to be saved. The bed’s silk rippled like it was trying to escape.
Even the women around her felt the pressure weighing over them, threatening their very existence.
And Amaya’s dark black eyes shined sharply—
Possessively.
Hungrily.
The devourer took one step forward and that step alone erased more than half of the room out of existence.
Then, her eyes turned.
Not towards Shadow or Felberta, they turned in the direction where Allura was and the moment the devourer’s eyes locked into that direction,
Her eyes became... even more dangerous.
Almost as if she could see Allura through the space and her lips parted.
Denial.
Complete denial.
The devourer clenched her fists, her nails pressing into her palm so strongly that blood came out.
And her mind screamed a single thought, so clear that the rest of the women felt it even without trying to sense it through their Bond—
It should have been me.
Nux’s first child?
That title?
That closeness?
That bond?
Amaya wantedall of it.
She wanted Nux to look atherfirst.
She wanted him to reach forher instinctively.
She wanted to be hiscenter.
Even if she couldn’t have him alone—
She still wanted to be closest to him.
And a child was the closest thing in existence.
A piece of him.
A piece that stayed.
A piece no one could replace.
And when all these thoughts strengthened in her mind—
BOOOOOOOOOOM
Amaya’s aura flared again.
And this time, it wasn’t only emotion.
It was... intent.
Cold, direct, dangerousintent.
Shadow felt it first and her eyes widened.
Because Amaya’s killing intent wasn’t aimed at an enemy.
It was aimed at Allura.
The room went tense.
Aeliana’s gaze sharpened instantly, like a blade responding to another blade.
Lyriana’s eyes turned colder.
Edda and Aisha were surprised.
Riona was frozen.
Thyra and Rune’s bodies moved without thinking—half a step, positioning themselves.
Ember, Astaria, Melia and Vyriana narrowed their eyes, ready to act the moment Amaya did.
Even Skyla stopped smiling.
But before anything could happen—
Felberta stepped in front of Amaya and—
"Stop.
That is enough."

sentences.text: "Allura... she...
She is pregnant."
Shadow spoke with a shocked look on her face and for a heartbeat, nobody moved.
Then—
"...what?"
Skyla blurted out, her eyes wide in surprise.
Aeliana’s eyes widened sharply, then narrowed, like she didn’t believe it.
Felberta froze completely.
Lane’s hand rose to her lips.
Even Lyriana’s cold expression cracked for a second.
As for Amaya...
She froze.
Completely.
"...Pregnant?"
Felberta repeated, as if unsure of what she had just heard.
"Yes,"
Shadow nodded slowly.
"She’s pregnant."
And as the words settled into the room—
It was like time stopped.
The floating motes of starlight above the bed hung in place.
The galaxies painted on the walls slowed until they were barely moving.
Even the shadow-silk sheets around Shadow’s body stopped shifting, as if the room itself didn’t know how to react to news that big.
Then—
Felberta’s fingers twitched—like something inside her tried to grab the air and couldn’t.
Her wide... empty eyes stayed fixed on Shadow, as if her mind was refusing to accept the words.
Pregnant.
A child...
Nux’s child...
Felberta had been the first.
The first to find him.
The first to see him when he had nothing.
The first to make him hers, before the others appeared, before the family became what it was now.
She had to share him, yes.
And honestly, at this point, she didn’t mind.
She actually thought of these women like her sisters, people who kept her company all the time.
She was actually quite close to them and had accepted them all.
But...
Even then—
Her title still mattered, at least to her.
The First wife.
And in her heart, in a place she rarely showed, she had always believed something else would be first too.
His first child.
It was only right.
It was only fair.
Was it not?
Nux’s first child should have been hers by right.
And when she realized it wasn’t... she... was not happy.
To Felberta, this was important.
She had trained herself to not want it yet.
To not... reach for it yet.
After all, it wasn’t safe.
For a long time, their lives had been nothing but movement.
Running.
Hiding.
Fighting.
Challenging... the impossible.
Nux had been throwing himself at monsters that once had the power to erase him with a mere thought.
Be it the King of the Skyfall Kingdom, the Pseudo Sage of the Forgotten Continent, the Dragon Lord of Yrniel, or World Leaders of different Worlds they had been to.
When they first learned about them, these were all existences far stronger than any of them and even then—
Nux did not back down, he challenged them all.
Again and again.
Like he didn’t know fear.
Like he didn’t know the meaning of "too far."
And in a life like that—
Bringing a newborn child... would have been madness.
Sure, they were strong, maybe even strong enough to protect the child if they had to but...
A newborn baby is fragile.
A newborn baby needed time.
A newborn baby needed peace.
He needed a home that didn’t shake every day because the Universe itself was angry.
Felberta understood that earlier than most.
And she had held back.
Not once.
Not twice.
For years.
For... centuries even.
At their level, pregnancy wasn’t some accident that happened because passion got out of hand.
It was a choice.
They could decide.
They had learned that truth a long, long time ago—back when the System still wrapped around their lives like invisible chains and rules.
Back then, even during intimacy, the System pushed everything in one direction.
Nux’s ’fluids’ didn’t become a seed of life.
They became fuel.
It flowed into the women like pure nourishment, strengthening their cores, expanding their foundations, pushing their cultivation forward.
That was why, even after their intimate sessions were so... long, none of the women got pregnant.
Because the System gave the ’energy’ that Nux released a purpose.
And it wasn’t to create a child.
Later, after Nux broke free from the System’s grip—after their understanding deepened, after their bodies became more than the System’s rules—
They learned the other truth.
Theycouldstill get pregnant.
They simply had to allow it.
They had to stop the flow from being consumed as power... and let it become life.
It was a simple choice.
But...
It was also a choice that had a terrifying consequence.
A child in circumstances as unstable and dangerous as theirs?
With how protective Nux was of his Family, it would basically cripple all his movements.
And the women, even those who had thought about it and wanted it much more desperately than anyone else, understood it.
This was the reason Felberta and others always stopped themselves at the last moment.
Not yet.
Not while we’re still hunted.
Not while our enemies might come to us anytime.
Not while the Universe itself is shaking from anger.
These thoughts were how the women, especially Felberta, had lived, this was how she had survived.
And then—
Their Universe became complete.
A true base.
A true... home.
A place no outsider could find so easily.
A place wrapped in protection so deep that inside it they felt... untouchable.
And to some extent, they were.
Here, they had... close to absolute control.
And for the first time...
Felberta’s thoughts changed.
For the first time, it wasn’t... crazy anymore.
It became possible.
Felberta had started thinking:
Soon.
Maybe soon.
Maybe I’ll talk to Nux.
Maybe we can plan it together.
And no, it wasn’t because she wanted to ’win’ against the others.
Well, at some level, she did.
After all, Felberta too was selfish at some level.
But the much stronger reason was because she wanted to see—
She wanted to see Nux smile that way.
That soft smile.
The smile a father had when he held his child.
She wanted to see Nux carrying their child.
That thought alone made her heart feel at ease—
It was a feeling so strong that her mind refused to imagine it.
She wanted toseeit, for real.
Before anyone else.
But now—
Allura had taken a step forward.
And that "first" was gone.
Felberta’s chest tightened at that thought.
So much that for a long moment, she couldn’t move.
The entire room felt her emotion.
Of course, she wasn’t angry.
She did not hate Allura, she couldn’t possibly hate her sister.
She was just... frustrated.
A silent, bitter frustration that didn’t know where to go.
It just... sat inside her like a stone, refusing to diminish and Felberta... she remained silent.
What else could she even do?
Well, at least that was what the first wife thought.
But...
Not everyone had self-control as strong as hers.
Especially a certain devourer whose attachment to her husband was... quite distorted in a strange manner.
For a moment, just like the rest, Amaya was frozen.
Her dark eyes had gone blank, her body stiff, like someone had poured cold water into her very veins, numbing them down.
But then—
Amaya’s gaze sharpened and together with her gaze, the very air around her changed.
Then—
BOOOOOOOOOM
Her Aura exploded.
Ridiculous amounts of devouring energy gathered around her, devouring the very room they were in.
The light motes inside trembled, as if screaming, begging to be saved.
The bed’s silk rippled like it was trying to escape.
Even the women around her felt the pressure weighing over them, threatening their very existence.
And Amaya’s dark black eyes shined sharply—
Possessively.
Hungrily.
The devourer took one step forward and that step alone erased more than half of the room out of existence.
Then, her eyes turned.
Not towards Shadow or Felberta, they turned in the direction where Allura was and the moment the devourer’s eyes locked into that direction,
Her eyes became... even more dangerous.
Almost as if she could see Allura through the space and her lips parted.
Denial.
Complete denial.
The devourer clenched her fists, her nails pressing into her palm so strongly that blood came out.
And her mind screamed a single thought, so clear that the rest of the women felt it even without trying to sense it through their Bond—
It should have been me.
Nux’s first child?
That title?
That closeness?
That bond?
Amaya wantedall of it.
She wanted Nux to look atherfirst.
She wanted him to reach forher instinctively.
She wanted to be hiscenter.
Even if she couldn’t have him alone—
She still wanted to be closest to him.
And a child was the closest thing in existence.
A piece of him.
A piece that stayed.
A piece no one could replace.
And when all these thoughts strengthened in her mind—
BOOOOOOOOOOM
Amaya’s aura flared again.
And this time, it wasn’t only emotion.
It was... intent.
Cold, direct, dangerousintent.

Felberta stepped in front of Amaya and—
"Stop.
That is enough."

chapters.title: Chapter 2250: We need to tell him.
paragraphs: "Stop.
That is enough."

Felberta spoke as she looked into Amaya’s eyes with a strong, authoritative look on her face. The devourer looked at her with her dark, hollow, possessive eyes, almost as if she would even tear apart Felberta if she tried to stop her, and Felberta...
She wasn’t offended by that look.
Instead, she looked at Amaya with... understanding.
After all, she knew what the woman was feeling; she too felt the same. It was just that while she held it all inside her—
Amaya did the opposite.
Amaya let her madness breathe and took another step forward.
"I will—"
But before she could even complete her words, another woman moved.
Riona.
The woman placed her hand on her daughter’s shoulder, even when her entire body was surrounded by devouring energy that had already begun eating her.
But the mother did not care; she just looked into her daughter’s eyes, and the moment Amaya realized what was happening—
Her Aura trembled.
Riona looked at her with a calm, understanding look on her face and then—
"Amaya,"
She called out.
Amaya’s jaw tightened at her mother’s call, her entire body shaking as her Aura became... weaker.
But the next second—
BOOOOOOM
Her Aura exploded again.
For a second, it looked like she might explode anyway. Like she might throw Riona’s hand off and walk out to hunt Allura down.
But then Evane stepped in too, taking Amaya’s other hand, holding it gently like she was holding someone drowning.
"Please,"
Evane whispered.
Aisha’s lips pressed together.
Edda looked ready to snap.
Even Shadow—who had started this mess—sat up straighter, suddenly very awake, staring at Amaya like she was watching a knife hovering above the family’s throat.
Vyriana, Astaria, Aeliana watched too.
And Amaya...
Her eyes trembled.
Even when angry, she realized this wasn’t a line-up she could win against.
If it was a one-on-one battle she might have had a chance, but against Astaria, Vyriana, and Aeliana all facing her together?
It was impossible.
Even at her strongest, Amaya would not win. Not to mention there was still Shadow, who could simply lock her away if she wanted to and there would be nothing she could do about it.
And that realization made her breathing uneven.
In her head, the thoughts were wild.
If Allura disappears, the first child can still be mine.
If Allura... dies, the problem ends.
If something happens and Allura never gives birth—
Those thoughts made her Aura surge again but—
"Amaya, I said enough."

The woman spoke, her voice much sharper than before, and Amaya’s gaze—just as sharp—snapped towards the Eldraeth Progenitor. The ’reason’ in her eyes had already vanished, even if it was a battle she would never win, she still wanted to give it a go, ready to throw it all.
For a second, the two of them stared at each other like rival queens.
But then—
Felberta’s gaze changed.
It... softened.
No, it was more accurate to say that Felberta looked... tired.
As if she had already fought this battle inside herself.
"You think I don’t feel it?"
The Eldraeth Progenitor asked softly.
Her voice wasn’t shaking, but the women could feel her intense emotions.
"You think I didn’t want it?"
Amaya’s lips parted at those words and Felberta continued.
"I wanted it first too.
More than you do."
The moment those words were said, silence fell.
Felberta said what every woman present here wanted to say.
Who here did not wish to be the first?
Who here did not wish to see Nux carry their blood in his arms?
Who here did not wish to feel... even closer to him?
Every single woman present here had a few screws loose in their heads; every single one of them was crazy for the man they loved.

And every single one of them, the moment they realized Allura had conceived, was hurt. Some felt she had betrayed them; they had decided not to conceive collectively, breaking the rules without any discussion was no different than betrayal.

Some were just... angry; they even thought of attacking Allura and... getting rid of the child. And for the very, very short moment, their minds justified that. After all, Allura had betrayed them first.
But...
"But if you touch her..."
Felberta spoke in a heavy tone as she lifted her eyes and looked right into Amaya’s.
The words didn’t need to finish.
Everyone understood.
Everyone thought the same.
If Amaya harmed Allura, she wouldn’t just be attacking a sister.
She would be attacking Nux.
And that was the one thing none of them would ever let happen.
Amaya’s Aura trembled at those words, the devouring energy around her weakening, mostly because she didn’t wish to hurt her mother.
Her eyes, however, still burned. Her breathing became even faster.
She looked like she hated the world.
Like she hated herself.
Like she hated the... helplessness she was feeling.
Then—
Her Aura dropped even more. It still hadn’t fully disappeared yet, not fully.
But enough to show she was listening.
Felberta exhaled slowly. Then, very slowly, she forced her face into something else.
"Allura’s child... will be Nux’s child."
No one spoke; after all, none of them liked those words, not when every single one of them wanted to be in Allura’s place.
But then—
Felberta said something else.
"And Nux isours,"
The first wife spoke.
"So the child... will beourstoo."
Her gaze moved around the room—meeting each woman’s eyes. Clearly, her words weren’t just for Amaya, but for everyone present here.
And for the first time since the reveal, warmth returned.
Very little, almost flickering warmth, but it still returned.
Skyla smiled, thinking about how she would be holding one little Nux very soon. The very thought made her giggle.
Evane’s expression was just... beautiful.
Ridiculously beautiful.
The gentle smile and her motherly warmth completely countered Amaya’s dark expression.
Riona chuckled too; she too wanted to be... a mother again.
Aeliana’s expression eased slightly; it was still sharp since like Amaya, she did not like this feeling one bit, but she was now... less ready to strike.
Lane’s shoulders lowered; her thoughts weren’t clear, she had hidden them from the rest.
Even Lyriana’s cold stare softened by a fraction.
Amaya, however, still looked like she might break.
She stared at Felberta as if she didn’t understand how she could accept it.
How she could swallow that pain.
Felberta met her gaze.
And for the first time ever since the reveal, the first wife smiled. No, she wasn’t happy, Felberta wasn’t a robot who could just... abandon her emotions.
But she was sincere.
"We are a family,"
She repeated.
"And our family is about to have a new member."
The room stayed quiet.
Then Shadow swallowed, still shocked, still half naked, still sitting there like she had dropped a meteor into the room.
"...Nux is going to lose his mind,"
She whispered lightly.
Skyla’s mouth opened.
Then she grinned.
"He’s going to be so happy."
Aisha’s eyes turned distant; she still did not like how Allura had betrayed even her. Edda was the same and looked away; even then, her expression softened to some extent.
And Amaya—
Amaya’s eyes trembled again.
Her Aura flickered.
For a moment, it looked like she might cry.
Then she clenched her jaw, turned her face away and—
She clicked her tongue, hating the fact that she was even here.
But she didn’t leave.
She didn’t attack anyone, and that alone was the closest thing to acceptance Amaya could give right now.
Felberta took a slow breath.
Then she looked at Shadow again.
"Are you certain?"
She asked, one last time.
"Yes."
Shadow nodded slowly.
"Does... he know?"
She asked.
A question that made the rest of the women lift their eyes.
Nux shouldn’t know.
Because if he did...
It would mean that he too hid it from them...
And if that was true then...
They wouldn’t know how they would react.
But Shadow...
"I do not think so."
She shook her head.
"We are not asking what youthink."
Lyriana muttered in a cold voice.
Shadow looked at her with the same cold eyes in return and—
"I cannot read his mind.
And even if I could, I wouldn’t if he doesn’t want me to."
She answered directly.
Lyriana didn’t say anything; she... couldn’t.
And Shadow continued—
"But I know my husband. I do not need to read his mind to know what I know.
If he knew, he would tell us, because he would understand how much it would hurt us if he doesn’t.
So if you do not trust him,
That does not make it my problem."
Shadow spoke in a tone she almost never used. For a moment, her presence felt... abnormally large, and Lyriana...
She could only lower her head and clench her fists, not because she did not like the way Shadow was talking to her, but because she... hated herself for doubting Nux, even for a second.
"Stop."
Felberta spoke again.
"She was just desperate."
Shadow looked at the first wife and calmed down.
Then, Felberta glanced at the rest of the women and—
"We need to tell him."
The first wife declared.
